title: The real cost of building your own compliance
summary: Building compliance on general AI looks cheaper until you price in maintenance, governance risk, and the capacity your competitors are gaining while you're still in development.
body_text: Most law firms don’t set out to build a compliance platform. It starts with a general-purpose AI tool pointed at conflicts, a script someone wrote to help with intake, a spreadsheet that tracks outside counsel guidelines. None of it feels like a platform decision. Until two years pass and a senior analyst leaves, the script breaks, and nobody is sure who owns fixing it. General-purpose AI doesn’t know what a true conflict is Conflicts clearance, matter intake, and client obligations management run on a data model that general-purpose AI doesn’t have. That model encodes what counts as a true conflict for your firm, why a matter was passed, which relationships carry institutional weight, and how your rules apply when a new matter touches three jurisdictions and a prior lateral hire. A general-purpose model has none of that context. Pointing it at your compliance data doesn’t give it the legal compliance model — it gives you confident-sounding output with no audit trail and nothing defensible underneath it. Encoding a firm’s vocabulary, obligations, and methods into a general agent is years of work from scratch. That work is already done. Every change to regulations, client requirements, or AI models becomes your team’s problem Assume the build goes well on day one. The maintenance problem starts immediately. Client guidelines change. New AI model versions ship. Bar rules update. Every one of those changes requires someone inside the firm to own the update, test the logic, validate the output, and document the rationale for when a regulator or client asks. That’s permanent overhead — staffed by people whose time is almost certainly better spent on higher-value work. 97 of the AmLaw 100 run on Intapp. That installed base represents two decades of exactly this work: building and maintaining the compliance data model, the legal-specific architecture, the workflow integrations. Firms choosing to build instead are spending time and engineering resources to get to where the category already is, while bearing the maintenance burden indefinitely after arrival. The governance risk doesn’t show up in a project budget Every firm leader eventually has the same conversation about a firm-wide compliance agent: “How do I know it will respect the ethical walls, not hallucinate, not surface the wrong data, and produce an audit trail I can defend to a court or a partnership vote?” General AI vendors can’t answer those questions, because the answers require an architecture the firm runs on — not a model with a wrapper around it. General AI keeps the content of a document and strips the metadata around it. In a firm, the metadata is the compliance posture. Which partner is walled off? Which deal team has MNPI? Which documents are on litigation hold? Strip those tags and you haven’t built an assistant — you’ve built a breach. There’s also a second exposure in the same approach: to make a firm’s documents usable, general AI copies them into a new store outside the firm’s retention rules and access controls. A discovery request reaches it. A retention schedule does not. 33% of firms now use AI firmwide, up from 17% in 2025. In that environment, 76% of professionals still use AI tools their firm hasn’t sanctioned. A homegrown tool built on general AI doesn’t close that gap. It widens it in a different direction. The opportunity cost is what closes the argument Intapp Compliance with Celeste deploys agents that draft intake requests, construct conflicts search strategies, match corporate trees, and ingest outside counsel guidelines — absorbing the routine work that rising volume used to demand more people for. Every quarter a firm spends building is a quarter a competitor widens that gap. The build decision doesn’t just cost time and engineering. It costs the compounding capacity advantage that starts the day a competitor goes live. title: Why Invoice Approval Without Spending Limits Is a Financial Control Nightmare
summary: Invoice approval without spending thresholds lets large purchases slip through unchecked. Learn how tiered escalation rules protect your business from AP risk.
body_text: **TL;DR:** Without spending thresholds in your AP workflow, department staff can approve invoices of any amount — leaving Finance Directors unaware of large purchases until they hit the ledger. Tiered approval thresholds with automatic escalation reduce unauthorized spend exposure by up to 85%, cut approval cycle time by routing invoices to the right person the first time, and create a complete audit trail that satisfies internal controls and external audits. The Control Gap That Hides in Plain Sight In most mid-market companies, the accounts payable approval process looks functional on paper. Invoices are received, reviewed, approved, posted to the ERP. The finance team is busy, the suppliers get paid, and month-end closes. Nothing appears broken — until it does. The break usually comes in one of three ways: a department head approves a $40,000 equipment purchase that the Finance Director didn’t know about until the payment run. A junior operations manager signs off on a supplier invoice that is $8,000 over the original purchase order. Or a large recurring service charge gets approved automatically because it has always been approved, even though the contract was renegotiated six months ago. In each case, the root cause is the same: there are no amount-based approval thresholds enforcing who can authorize what. Everyone with approval access can approve everything. This is not rare. According to APQC benchmarking research , more than 40% of mid-market companies have no formal approval authority matrix in their AP process — meaning that spending authority is informal, inconsistently applied, and unverifiable in an audit. The financial exposure this creates compounds with invoice volume. A company processing 100 invoices per month without thresholds has 100 opportunities per month for unauthorized spend to slip through unchallenged. This guide explains the specific control failures that emerge when invoice approval has no thresholds, how tiered escalation rules close each gap, and what a properly configured approval authority matrix looks like in practice for field service and environmental services businesses. The Anatomy of Uncontrolled Invoice Approval Before examining the failure modes, it is worth mapping what uncontrolled approval actually looks like in practice — because in many organizations it is not chaotic. It is quietly dysfunctional. The typical pattern in a mid-market service business: Invoices arrive in a shared finance inbox The accounts team identifies the approver based on who raised the purchase or manages the budget The approver receives the invoice (by email, hard copy, or both) and marks it approved The accounts team posts it to the ERP Nowhere in this flow is there a rule that says: if this invoice is over $10,000, it must also go to the Finance Director. The approver’s seniority determines the spending limit only by convention — which means the limit changes depending on who is available, who is in the office, and how much pressure the accounts team is under to close out the batch. The result is a three-way failure: Failure Mode What Happens Business Impact Over-routing to senior leaders All invoices go to Finance Director regardless of amount Bottleneck — strategic work delayed by invoice queue Under-routing to junior approvers Department staff approve high-value invoices without senior sign-off Unauthorized spend, compliance failure Inconsistent routing Same invoice type routed differently each time depending on who’s available No audit trail, no repeatable process Each of these failure modes can be eliminated with a properly configured approval authority matrix. The key is that the routing decision must be made by the system — not by the accounts clerk. Pain Point 1: Senior Leaders Either See Everything or Nothing In waste management, environmental services, facilities management, and other field-intensive businesses, Finance Directors and CFOs face a paradox in AP approval. Without thresholds, the organization chooses — often informally — one of two approaches: Approach A: Route everything to the Finance Director. This eliminates the risk of unauthorized spend but creates a severe bottleneck. A Finance Director processing 100 invoices per month spends an estimated 8-10 hours on routine approvals that should never require their attention. More critically, it means their approval queue is permanently cluttered with $200 stationery invoices sitting alongside $50,000 equipment contracts. Both wait the same amount of time, and neither gets the attention it deserves. Approach B: Give department managers blanket authority. This eliminates the bottleneck but removes control. An operations manager in the field can approve a $35,000 subcontractor invoice with the same authority they use to approve a $300 fuel charge. The Finance Director finds out about the $35,000 commitment only when the payment run is prepared — after the liability is already created. The solution is neither approach — it is a tiered system where the routing decision is determined by the invoice amount, not by availability or convention. Sample Approval Authority Matrix for a Mid-Market Service Business Invoice Amount Required Approver Escalation If No Action Under $1,000 (PO-matched) Auto-approved — Under $1,000 (non-PO) Department manager Finance Manager after 24h $1,000 – $10,000 Department manager Finance Director after 48h $10,000 – $50,000 Finance Director CFO after 48h Over $50,000 CFO / Board sign-off — With this structure, the Finance Director’s inbox contains only invoices that genuinely require their attention. Department managers retain meaningful authority without having unconstrained access to high-value approvals. And every routing decision is documented, timestamped, and auditable. For a deeper look at how AP approval workflows are structured, see our complete guide to AP approval workflow automation . Pain Point 2: Invoice-vs-PO Variance With No Escalation Rule A purchase order is a financial commitment. When a supplier invoice arrives for more than the PO amount, that excess represents unauthorized spend — unless someone with authority explicitly approves the variance. In organizations without variance escalation rules, what typically happens is this: the accounts team notices the discrepancy, but approving the original PO amount already went through the correct approver. Rather than restart the approval cycle, the team posts the invoice at the full invoiced amount and notes the variance in a spreadsheet for review at month-end. By month-end, there are 15 such variances to review, and most get approved retrospectively because the goods or services have already been delivered. This pattern means that invoice-vs-PO variances are approved by no one with actual authority — they are approved by administrative convenience. Auto PO matching addresses the detection side: the system identifies the variance automatically. But detection without escalation is insufficient. The escalation rule is what ensures the variance reaches the right approver before payment is released. A well-configured variance escalation rule specifies: The tolerance band (e.g., invoices within 5% of PO amount auto-approved; above 5% escalates) The absolute dollar cap (e.g., variances over $500 always escalate regardless of percentage) The target approver for variance review (typically one level above the original PO approver) Impact of PO Variance Without Escalation Rules Variance Scenario Without Rules With Rules Invoice 3% over PO ($300 on a $10,000 PO) Posted silently Auto-approved within tolerance Invoice 12% over PO ($1,200 on a $10,000 PO) Posted by accounts clerk Escalated to Finance Director Invoice 30% over PO ($3,000 on a $10,000 PO) Posted after month-end Blocked pending CFO approval Invoice with no matching PO Routed manually, often delayed Auto-rejected, vendor notified According to IOFM research on AP controls , organizations with automated PO variance escalation reduce unauthorized overpayment by an average of 73% compared to those relying on manual variance review. Pain Point 3: No Visibility Into Pending High-Value Approvals When there are no approval thresholds, there is also no way to prioritize the approval queue by financial risk. A $50,000 invoice sits in the same queue as a $150 utility bill, and both are equally invisible to the Finance Director until the accounts team manually calls attention to them. The practical consequence in field service and waste management businesses — where approvers are frequently in vehicles, at customer sites, or managing operational emergencies — is that high-value invoices are among the least likely to be actioned promptly. The approver’s phone buzzes with the same generic approval request regardless of the invoice amount. With amount-based threshold routing, the Finance Director receives only the invoices that meet their threshold, with a notification that clearly indicates the invoice value. Mobile approval interfaces allow them to act from the field without returning to the office. And automated escalation ensures that if they do not act within the defined window, the invoice escalates to the next authority level or is flagged for urgent follow-up. This transforms approval from a passive queue into an active priority system. The visibility improvement extends to dashboards: finance teams can monitor all invoices above a set threshold in real time, sorted by amount, age, and approval status. According to McKinsey’s research on finance operations digitization , real-time AP visibility reduces invoice processing exceptions by 30-40% and shortens payment cycle time by an average of four days. Pain Point 4: Approval Bypassing Under Operational Pressure In field service and environmental services businesses, operational continuity sometimes creates pressure to bypass approval controls. A waste removal contractor threatens to suspend service unless an overdue invoice is paid by end of day. A critical equipment hire company needs sign-off before they release the equipment to the job site. A fuel supplier puts the account on hold pending payment of a disputed invoice. In these situations, finance teams under pressure may verbally authorize payments, approve invoices retroactively, or bypass the approval system entirely to keep operations running. Without threshold enforcement, there is no mechanism to prevent this — or to document it when it happens. The result is a pattern that Gartner’s AP control research identifies as one of the top three sources of AP fraud and error in mid-market companies: retrospective approval of invoices that were paid without proper authorization, covered by after-the-fact documentation that satisfies neither internal audit nor external regulators. Threshold-based approval with mobile escalation resolves the operational pressure problem without sacrificing control. The Finance Director can approve a high-priority $25,000 invoice from their phone in two minutes if it is escalated with appropriate urgency flagging. The payment can be expedited while maintaining a complete, compliant approval trail. The choice is no longer between operational continuity and financial control — it is both. Pain Point 5: No Audit Trail for Spending Authority When invoice approval operates without thresholds, the audit trail documents what happened but not whether it was authorized correctly. An auditor reviewing the AP ledger can see that Invoice #INV-4429 for $22,000 was approved by the facilities manager — but cannot determine whether that facilities manager had authority to approve invoices above $10,000, because there is no policy record against which to evaluate the decision. This creates two audit risks: Internal audit failure : Internal controls cannot be verified if the policy is not documented and enforced systematically External regulatory risk : In regulated industries, unauthorized spend approvals can trigger compliance findings and financial penalties With a configured authority matrix, every approval carries a policy reference: the system records not just who approved the invoice, but under which policy rule they were authorized to do so. If the invoice exceeded the approver’s threshold, the system either escalated it or blocked it — and that decision is documented in the audit log. The audit trail also captures escalations and time-to-approval by tier — data that Deloitte’s AP transformation research identifies as increasingly required by both internal audit teams and external reviewers in service industries with high operational spend. What Tiered Invoice Approval Thresholds Look Like With AP Automation A modern accounts payable automation platform allows finance administrators to configure approval thresholds through a no-code policy builder — no IT involvement required. The configuration covers: Dollar threshold tiers with named approver roles at each level Vendor-specific approval rules (stricter thresholds for new vendors or strategic suppliers) PO variance tolerance bands with escalation targets Time-window escalation (auto-escalate if no action within 24/48/72 hours) Mobile approval notifications with invoice details and one-click approve/reject ERP sync on full approval (invoice posts to SAP, NetSuite, or other integrated system automatically) The AI-powered invoice capture layer reads the invoice amount from the document automatically, applies the correct threshold rule, and routes it without any manual intervention from the accounts team. For non-PO invoices, GL coding is applied automatically based on vendor history before the invoice reaches the approver — so approvers see pre-coded invoices and simply confirm or override. For further reading on how non-PO invoice processing fits into this workflow, see our guide on non-PO invoice processing challenges and solutions . The Business Case: What Threshold Automation Delivers The ROI of threshold-based approval automation operates across three dimensions: cost reduction, risk reduction, and cycle time improvement. AP Automation Outcomes — Threshold Enforcement Metric Manual (No Thresholds) Automated (With Thresholds) Improvement Unauthorized spend incidents per year 8-15 1-2 ~85% reduction Average approval cycle time 3-5 days Under 24 hours 75-80% faster Finance Director time on routine approvals 8-10 hrs/month Under 1 hr/month ~90% reduction PO variance incidents detected 30-40% 95-100% Near-complete detection Audit findings related to approval controls 3-6 per cycle 0-1 per cycle Significant reduction Early-payment discounts captured Under 20% 60-80% 3-4x improvement According to Gartner’s finance automation data , organizations that implement structured approval authority matrices with automated routing achieve payback on their AP automation investment within 6-12 months, primarily through unauthorized spend prevention and early-payment discount capture. The early-payment discount opportunity is particularly significant. Faster approval cycles — enabled by threshold routing that sends invoices to the right person the first time — mean more invoices are approved within the early-payment window (typically 10 days from receipt). For a company processing $500,000 in monthly AP, capturing an average 1.5% early-payment discount on 60% of invoices represents $4,500 per month, or $54,000 annually. Our Verdict: When to Implement Tiered Approval Thresholds Tiered invoice approval thresholds with auto-escalation are appropriate for: Companies processing 30+ invoices per month with multiple approvers Organizations where Finance Directors or CFOs currently review routine low-value invoices Businesses where department managers have informal but unconstrained approval authority Companies in regulated industries requiring documented spending control frameworks Organizations that have experienced unauthorized spend, duplicate payments, or AP audit findings Manual approval without thresholds may remain workable only for very small businesses with fewer than 20 invoices per month and a single approver who reviews all transactions personally. If your organization is beyond that scale, the cost of uncontrolled approval — in unauthorized spend, audit exposure, and Finance Director time — almost certainly exceeds the cost of implementing a threshold framework. The configuration effort is low: a standard authority matrix with three to five tiers can be configured in a modern AP platform within a single working day. The ongoing maintenance is minimal — threshold levels are updated as the business grows or organizational structures change, typically once or twice per year. Conclusion Invoice approval without spending limits is not a gap that finance teams notice in real time — it is one they discover retrospectively, when an unauthorized purchase appears on the ledger, when an auditor flags a control weakness, or when a Finance Director realizes they have been approving $300 invoices alongside $30,000 equipment contracts for months. Tiered approval thresholds with automatic escalation remove the ambiguity from spending authority. They route each invoice to the right approver the first time, enforce PO variance controls, prevent unauthorized high-value approvals, and create the audit trail that modern finance operations require. If your AP process currently operates without a formal authority matrix, the fastest path to financial control is to define your threshold tiers, configure them in your AP automation platform, and let the system enforce the rules automatically — from the day the invoice arrives to the moment it posts to your ERP. See how Peakflo configures tiered invoice approval thresholds for field service and environmental services businesses. Frequently Asked Questions What is an invoice approval threshold? An invoice approval threshold is a spending limit that determines which approver must authorize an invoice based on its value. For example, invoices under $5,000 may be approved by a department manager, while invoices over $20,000 require Finance Director sign-off. Thresholds enforce spending authority without requiring senior leaders to review every transaction. What is AP approval escalation? AP approval escalation is the automatic routing of an invoice to a higher-authority approver when certain conditions are met — such as the invoice amount exceeding a threshold, the invoice value exceeding the original PO amount by a set percentage, or the original approver not responding within a defined time window. Escalation is triggered automatically by the AP system without manual intervention. What is an approval authority matrix? An approval authority matrix is a structured table that maps spending limits to approver roles. It defines who can authorize invoices at each dollar tier — for example, department managers approve up to $10,000, finance managers up to $50,000, and the CFO above $50,000. A well-designed matrix ensures that spending control is enforced consistently across the organization. How does invoice-vs-PO variance escalation work? Invoice-vs-PO variance escalation triggers when a supplier invoice arrives with an amount higher than the original purchase order. The system calculates the variance as a percentage or absolute dollar difference. If the variance exceeds a configured tolerance — such as 5% or $500 — the invoice is automatically escalated to a senior approver for review before payment is authorized. What happens if no approval thresholds are configured? Without configured approval thresholds, two failure modes occur: either all invoices route to the most senior approver regardless of amount (creating a bottleneck), or all approvers have blanket authority regardless of invoice value (creating a control gap). Both scenarios increase financial risk — one delays payment cycles, the other allows unauthorized spend to pass unchecked. Can invoice approval thresholds be set by vendor as well as amount? Yes. Modern AP automation platforms allow approval rules to be configured by multiple dimensions simultaneously — invoice amount, vendor category, cost center, department, expense type, and PO status. This allows businesses to apply stricter approval requirements for new or unverified vendors, strategic suppliers, or capital expenditure categories. How do approval thresholds help with audit compliance? Approval thresholds create a complete, timestamped audit trail showing which approver authorized each invoice, at what amount, and under which policy. This satisfies internal audit requirements and external regulatory reviews by demonstrating that spending authority was correctly applied at every transaction level. Without thresholds, auditors cannot verify that appropriate authorization was obtained. What is the difference between single-level and multi-level invoice approval? Single-level approval routes every invoice to one approver regardless of amount. Multi-level approval uses thresholds to route invoices sequentially through multiple approvers — for example, department manager first, then Finance Director if over a set amount. Multi-level approval is more appropriate for organizations with diverse spend categories and different risk tolerances by transaction size. How long does it take to configure invoice approval thresholds? Configuring invoice approval thresholds in a modern AP automation platform typically takes 2-4 hours for a standard authority matrix with 3-5 approval tiers. More complex configurations involving multiple cost centers, vendor categories, or department-specific rules may require 1-2 days of setup. Most platforms provide no-code policy builders that allow finance administrators to configure rules without IT support. Can approval thresholds be applied to purchase orders as well as invoices? Yes. Best practice is to apply spending thresholds at both the PO creation stage and the invoice approval stage. PO thresholds prevent unauthorized purchase commitments; invoice thresholds ensure that any variance between PO and invoice is reviewed by the appropriate authority. Applying controls at both stages creates a complete procure-to-pay governance framework. See our three-way matching guide for how PO controls and invoice matching work together. What industries benefit most from tiered invoice approval thresholds? Industries with high invoice volumes, diverse spend categories, and field-based operations benefit most from tiered approval thresholds. These include waste management, environmental services, facilities management, logistics and freight, construction, field service, healthcare, and manufacturing. In these industries, operational managers frequently approve invoices while working remotely — making digital threshold enforcement and mobile approval essential.

title: San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District Launches 24/7 Voice AI for Resident Service Requests
summary: In its first month live, EffiGov's voice AI answered 816 calls around the clock, resolving about half on its own and filing 207 service requests straight into the district's system.
body_text: San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District Launches 24/7 Voice AI for Resident Service Requests Stockton, CA – August 10, 2026 The San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District has launched a 24/7 voice AI line with EffiGov, giving residents always-on access to report mosquito problems, request inspections, and reach district staff at any hour. Native integration Every request the agent takes is geo-verified in Esri ArcGIS and filed as a Survey123 record, straight into the tools the district’s field crews already use, with no staff rekeying. Esri ArcGIS Geo-verify the address Survey123 File the request as a record Serving more than 790,000 residents across San Joaquin County, the district fields a heavy, seasonal call volume, from mosquito complaints and requests for mosquito fish to green-pool reports and dead-bird questions. Like most vector control agencies, it runs on finite field and office staff while demand climbs through the summer. The district went fully live, around the clock, on July 8, 2026, and the numbers followed fast. Calls now resolve in a median of just over a minute. In the first month, by the numbers 816 Calls answered ~50% Ticket created or resolved via Q&A 207 Service requests filed ~70% Kept off the front desk ” In our first 30 days, EffiGov helped us handle a record month of service requests without adding a single position. Instead of sitting at a desk answering phones, our technicians are out in the field doing the work residents actually need. And residents are getting clear, helpful answers the moment they call, at any hour, which is exactly the experience we want to give them. Omar Khweiss District Manager, San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District Before launch, EffiGov worked closely with district staff to mirror existing workflows, reviewing live calls together each week and tuning the agent so residents get accurate, consistent information about what the district does and does not do. "When mosquito season hits, every call is someone with a real problem in their yard," said Aubteen Pour-Biazar, Co-Founder and CEO of EffiGov. "The district trusted us with the first thing a resident hears, and we're proud it now answers every one of those calls, day or night, and gets the request to the field team without anyone waiting on hold." ” The visibility is what won me over. I can pull up any call, hear exactly how the agent handled it, and shape how it responds going forward. It reliably takes the routine questions and requests off our plate, it has caught things we would have missed, and it freed our team from being tied to the phones. Christina Falk GIS/IT Coordinator, San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District About the San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District The San Joaquin County Mosquito and Vector Control District protects public health across San Joaquin County, California, monitoring and controlling mosquitoes and other vectors and responding to resident service requests countywide. Learn more at sjmosquito.org . About EffiGov EffiGov builds voice AI for local governments, starting with 311 and non-emergency call handling. Founded in 2025, the company helps governments deliver responsive service while allowing staff to focus on work that requires human expertise. Learn more at effigov.com . Media Contact: press@effigov.com

title: Array Labs, Esper Satellite Imagery Announce Strategic Partnership to Co-Enrich Data
summary: Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery will co-enrich imagery to deliver a real-time, data-rich 3D map of Earth. Together, the two are committed to providing advanced, actionable, and affordable geospatial products to customers, driving growth in the commercial and government sectors alike.
body_text: Palo Alto, California, and Melbourne, Australia, March 13, 2024 – Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery today announced a strategic partnership to co-enrich each other's products, creating a powerful, one-of-a-kind dataset that combines high-resolution 3D with cutting-edge hyperspectral. The co-enrichment commitment allows both companies to provide even more value to their respective customers and markets. Under the terms of this agreement, users of Esper’s low-cost, extended-spectrum hyperspectral satellite imaging platform will be able to receive combined high-resolution 3D data. Similarly, Array’s customers will be able to combine and receive hyperspectral imagery with their 3D data purchases or subscriptions. This first-of-its-kind collaboration will empower customers to unlock previously unattainable insights, as they gain access to a comprehensive, multidimensional view of the Earth’s surface. By fusing Array Labs’ centimeter-level 3D data with Esper’s rich hyperspectral imagery, customers will not only be able to measure volumetric changes at scale, but also identify the precise materials driving those changes. The impact of this partnership will be felt across sectors: BUILDING A REAL-TIME, DATA-RICH 3D MAP OF EARTH Array’s constellation, consisting of dozens of miniaturized, cost-effective radar satellites, is set to deliver a view of Earth in intricate 3D, with details down to the centimeter and unprecedented revisit rates. Meanwhile, Esper’s highly unique hyperspectral imagers capture up to 217 spectral bands at a remarkable 6-meter resolution, revisiting every corner of the globe every 10 days. Esper launched its first spacecraft – Over the Rainbow – last week aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-10 mission, with just under $1 million in pre-seed funding, the company told TechCrunch . Array Labs can confirm it will be launching its first three demonstrators – Kaladin, Rock, and Lopin – on Transporter-11 in just a few months. Around the same time, Esper will launch its second demonstrator with India’s ISRO. "Esper provides an immense spectral range not provided by others, very frequent revisit, and shares our passion for bringing high-value data from space in a highly affordable manner," said Array Labs CEO Andrew Peterson. "To our knowledge, this will be the first time 3D and hyperspectral imaging are combined and delivered from space for commercial use." "Esper and Array share the same ideology of launching with as low of a cost and as quickly as possible that challenges a lot of the status quo in the Earth Observation industry,” said Esper CEO Shoaib Iqbal. “This partnership further cements that, with a focus on the value both our companies can deliver together to solve customer problems." Together, Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery are committed to delivering the most advanced, actionable, and affordable geospatial products to customers, driving growth and innovation in the commercial and government sectors alike.

title: Salesforce Agentic Enterprise Index: Agent Deployments More Than Double Year over Year

body_text: Open Image Modal Image Modal Customer Zero: Slackbot at Salesforce Salesforce’s AI agent in Slack — Slackbot — is the fastest-adopted tool in Salesforce history. title: Airbnb.org offers free emergency housing to people displaced by wildfires in Washington state
summary: Airbnb.org, a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is partnering with Washington 211 to offer free emergency housing to residents displaced by several active wildfires across six Washington counties and three tribal communities.
body_text: Airbnb.org , a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is partnering with Washington 211 to offer free emergency housing to residents displaced by several active wildfires across six Washington counties and three tribal communities. Stays are free for guests and are funded by Airbnb.org and the generosity of donors. “When disaster strikes, a comfortable place to call home can make all the difference, while providing first responders an opportunity to recharge for the next day,” said Christoph Gorder, Executive Director of Airbnb.org. “We’re grateful to work with our partners to help people displaced by the wildfires find a free temporary place to call home as their recovery process begins. ” “Washington 211 has long been the front door to help in Washington—and now, thanks to our partnership with Airbnb.org, that includes temporary housing for people who are displaced or lost their homes,” said Deb Miller, Washington 211 Board Chair. “As the provider of 211 in Washington, Crisis Connections is committed to ensuring those impacted by the devastating wildfires are connected to essential resources in their community. Through this partnership, 211 can now offer something no one should have to go without—a safe place to sleep tonight,” said Michelle McDaniel, CEO, Crisis Connections. How it works Airbnb.org partners with local organizations before disaster strikes, so housing support is available quickly. Washington 211 is identifying residents in need of temporary housing and referring them to Airbnb.org, which provides credits to book a nearby Airbnb stay that meets their needs—often close to their workplaces, schools, or support networks. Temporary housing is available to residents in the following counties and tribal communities who are displaced by wildfires: Spokane, Stevens, Chelan, Okanogan, Yakima and Ferry counties Spokane, Colville and Yakima tribal communities To determine eligibility, displaced residents should call 211 between the hours of 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Pacific Time. A specialist will provide personalized support throughout the referral process. How to help Anyone interested in supporting those impacted by the wildfires in Washington can help by donating to Airbnb.org. 100 percent of donations go directly toward connecting people in crisis with emergency housing. If you’re an Airbnb host, you can sign up to provide discounted Airbnb.org stays. Airbnb.org in Washington Since its founding in 2020, Airbnb.org has provided nearly 17,000 nights of free emergency housing in Washington. Following the Skagit River flooding in December 2025, Airbnb.org and Washington 211 partnered to provide nearly 1,300 nights of free emergency housing.

Launches Financial Institutions Investment Banking Group August 4, 2026 Download (opens in new window) New team expands M&A, capital raising, and valuation capabilities for banks, credit unions, and other financial services entities Memphis, TN — August 4, 2026 — FHN Financial Securities Corp. today announced the creation of a Financial Institutions Investment Banking Group (FIG) with the addition of Andrew Christians and Greg Cunningham, who previously led the FIG Banking practice of Donnelly Penman & Partners (DPP), along with other DPP FIG Banking team members. DPP was supportive of the transition to FHN Financial. The team provides merger and acquisition (M&A), capital raising, and business valuation services to financial institutions, including banks and credit unions, and other financial services entities. This addition further enhances FHN Financial’s extensive platform of products and services focused on serving the needs of depository financial institutions. “By integrating a proven FIG practice with our platform, clients have access to a single partner for M&A, capital formation, and a range of balance sheet management solutions — strengthening our ability to help institutions navigate strategic decisions.” said Tim Romanow, President of FHN Financial. Christians and Cunningham have a strong record in providing capital raising, M&A, and financial advisory services to banks and credit unions of all sizes, as well as non-depository financial services companies (including commercial finance, mortgage banking, FinTech, trust and wealth, and consumer finance). Their deep relationships with depository leadership and boards, high net worth investors, family offices, and bank focused institutional investors provide meaningful value to customers. “We are excited to join FHN Financial. Through extensive interaction with the leadership team of this storied organization, it is clear we share the same “client-first” culture. Our team has spent our careers serving financial institutions. At FHN Financial, we can deliver the same hands-on approach with broader distribution and an expanded toolkit to solve complex needs. We are confident this is the right partnership to best assist our clients for years to come.” said Andrew Christians, Managing Director and Co-Head, Financial Institutions Banking Group, FHN Financial. “As the financial institutions landscape continues to evolve, we recognized an opportunity existed to better serve our clients by partnering with a firm that not only shares our commitment to excellence and results, but expands the depth of offerings we can provide," said Greg Cunningham, Managing Director and Co-Head, Financial Institutions Banking Group. "FHN Financial's outstanding reputation, values-based culture, and proven track record stood out as we worked more closely with the leadership team. Joining FHN will enable us to expand the breadth of solutions we offer, enhance the value we deliver to clients, and create new opportunities for long-term growth." FHN Financial is a leading capital markets firm serving a range of institutional, municipal, and corporate customers across the globe. As a division of First Horizon Bank, FHN Financial combines enterprise-scale resources with specialized expertise. FHN Financial’s various business lines deliver a full suite of fixed income products, strategies, services, and balance sheet management solutions. Learn more at fhnfinancial.com . title: Tribunal Federal de Apelaciones invalida unánimemente la ley de censura de Puerto Rico aprobada durante la pandemia de COVID-19
summary: La ley coartaba la labor periodística en medio de la pandemia de COVID-19 y amenazaba la libertad de prensa durante periodos de emergencias declaradas
body_text: Tribunal Federal de Apelaciones invalida unánimemente la ley de censura de Puerto Rico aprobada durante la pandemia de COVID-19 La ley coartaba la labor periodística en medio de la pandemia de COVID-19 y amenazaba la libertad de prensa durante periodos de emergencias declaradas Case : Rodríguez-Cotto v. Pierluisi-Urrutia Affiliate : ACLU of Puerto Rico August 4, 2026 4:52 pm ACLU Affiliate ACLU of Puerto Rico National Chapter Spokesperson Brian Hauss › ACLU Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project Media Contact media@aclu.org (212) 549-2666 125 Broad Street 18th Floor New York, NY 10004 United States SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — En una decisión unánime, el Tribunal de Apelaciones del Primer Circuito de Estados Unidos anuló la ley de Puerto Rico de 2020 contra las llamadas "noticias falsas", al considerarla una regulación inconstitucional basada en el contenido que restringe la libertad de expresión protegida. Dos periodistas impugnaron la ley, argumentando que amenazaba con coartar cualquier reportaje que pudiera perjudicar la imagen del gobierno durante una emergencia. "Como periodista independiente en Puerto Rico, mi trabajo es buscar la verdad y exigir responsabilidades a quienes ostentan el poder, especialmente cuando surge una crisis y el público necesita información transparente y confiable", afirmó la periodista Sandra Rodríguez. “La ley de ‘noticias falsas’ de Puerto Rico era una amenaza constante. La decisión de hoy del Tribunal de Apelaciones del Primer Circuito es una victoria no solo para mí o la prensa, sino para todos los ciudadanos en Puerto Rico. Este fallo garantiza que podemos seguir haciendo nuestro trabajo —investigando, cuestionando e informando— sin temor a ser criminalizados por buscar la verdad”. “Este caso va más allá del ejercicio del periodismo. Esto atenta contra el significado mismo de vivir en una sociedad democrática donde las personas tienen derecho a expresarse libremente sin temor a ser silenciadas por el Estado”, declaró, por su parte, el periodista Rafelli González Cotto. “Agradezco al tribunal por defender la Primera Enmienda no solo para los periodistas, sino para todos los ciudadanos de Puerto Rico”. La ley de Puerto Rico de 2020 tipificaba como delito dar a sabiendas una “falsa alarma” sobre catástrofes inminentes o transmitir a sabiendas información falsa sobre cualquier tema cuando hacerlo resultara en un riesgo inminente para la seguridad, la salud o la propiedad. Quienes infringieran la ley se enfrentaban a penas de hasta tres años de cárcel y una multa de hasta $5,000 dólares. "La función de vigilancia de la prensa nunca es más importante ni está más en peligro que durante una emergencia", declaró Brian Hauss, subdirector del Proyecto de Libertad de Expresión, Privacidad y Tecnología de la ACLU. "Agradecemos que el tribunal haya declarado inconstitucional esta ley de 'noticias falsas', que amenazaba con silenciar al periodismo independiente precisamente cuando la ciudadanía más lo necesita". La demanda, presentada originalmente durante la crisis de salud por el COVID-19, fue interpuesta por la Unión Americana de Libertades Civiles (ACLU) y la ACLU de Puerto Rico en nombre de dos periodistas, Sandra Rodríguez Cotto y Rafelli González Cotto, quienes temían que la ley se utilizara para castigarlos por su cobertura de emergencias públicas, especialmente por reportajes que perjudicaran la imagen del gobierno. "Celebramos esta victoria que protege dos de nuestros derechos más fundamentales: la libertad de prensa y la libertad de expresión", afirmó Fermín Arraiza Navas, director legal de la ACLU de Puerto Rico. "Esta ley nefasta, firmada inicialmente por el exgobernador Ricardo Rosselló y enmendada por una legislatura en decadencia con la aprobación de la gobernadora Wanda Vázquez en La Fortaleza, solo tenía como norte criminalizar la disidencia y perseguir a la prensa en tiempos de emergencia por simplemente discrepar del discurso oficialista. No lo permitiremos". El 31 de marzo de 2023, el Tribunal de Distrito de los Estados Unidos para el Distrito de Puerto Rico dictó una orden judicial permanente contra la ley, al considerar que su alcance excesivamente amplio conllevaba el riesgo de enjuiciamientos politizados y de coartar la libertad de expresión protegida en asuntos de interés público. Este martes, 4 de agosto, el Tribunal de Apelaciones del Primer Circuito de los Estados Unidos confirmó la decisión, dictaminando que la ley viola la Primera Enmienda porque impone una restricción basada en el contenido a la libertad de expresión protegida sin justificación suficiente. El tribunal señaló que la ley carece de las limitaciones esenciales incluidas en otras leyes sobre falsas alarmas, y que podría utilizarse para procesar a quienes se oponen a la postura del gobierno en debates sobre temas controvertidos como la eficacia de las mascarillas durante la pandemia de COVID-19, así como en relación con chistes, sátira o ficción. Como escribió el tribunal, la ley de Puerto Rico “representa una restricción inadmisible de la libertad de expresión, especialmente en tiempos de emergencia, cuando es imperativo que el público esté bien informado y que el gobierno rinda cuentas”. “Con esta ley, el Gobierno de Puerto Rico puso en peligro el derecho a la libertad de expresión y la libertad de prensa, protecciones que son cada vez más indispensables”, declaró Annette Martínez Orabona, directora ejecutiva de la ACLU de Puerto Rico. “Esto también fue un intento de desalentar la fiscalización justa y necesaria del gobierno, precisamente durante periodos de emergencia como el que Puerto Rico vive en la actualidad, con una crisis en el servicio de agua potable. Se trata de derechos que están siendo atacados desde múltiples frentes y que hoy logramos proteger”. Puedes leer la opinión aquí . También puedes leer más sobre la ley aquí . Previous press release about this case Federal Appeals Court Unanimously Strikes Down Puerto Rico’s COVID-Era Censorship Law August 4, 2026 4:37 pm Related Issues Freedom of the Press Free Speech Related Content Press Release Aug 2026 Free Speech Federal Appeals Court Unanimously Strikes Down Puerto Rico’s COVID-Era Censorship Law SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — In a unanimous decision, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit struck down Puerto Rico’s 2020 “fake news” law, holding that the law is an unconstitutional content-based regulation of protected speech. Two journalists challenged the law, saying it threatened to chill any reporting during an emergency that may reflect poorly on the government. “As an independent journalist in Puerto Rico, my job is to seek the truth and hold those in power accountable—especially when crisis hits and the public needs transparent, reliable information most,” said journalist Sandra Rodriguez. “Puerto Rico’s 'fake news' law hung over our heads like a constant threat. Today’s decision by the First Circuit Court of Appeals is a victory not just for me or the press, but for every citizen in Puerto Rico. This ruling ensures that we can continue doing our jobs—investigating, questioning, and reporting—without fear of being criminalized for seeking the truth.” “This case goes beyond the practice of journalism. It strikes at the very meaning of living in a democratic society where people have the right to express themselves freely without fear of being silenced by the state,” said journalist Rafelli González Cotto. "I am grateful to the court for defending the First Amendment not only for journalists, but for all citizens of Puerto Rico.” The 2020 Puerto Rico law made it a crime to knowingly raise a “false alarm” about impending catastrophes or knowingly convey false information on any topic when doing so results in an imminent risk to safety, health, property; those found in violation of the law faced up to three years in jail and a fine of up to $5,000. “The watchdog function of the press is never more important, or more in danger, than during an emergency,” said Brian Hauss, deputy director of the ACLU’s Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project. “We’re grateful that the court struck down this unconstitutional ‘fake news’ law, which threatened to muzzle independent journalism precisely when the public needs it most.” Originally filed during the COVID-19 public health crisis, the American Civil Liberties Union and the ACLU of Puerto Rico filed the lawsuit on behalf of two journalists, Sandra Rodríguez Cotto and Rafelli González Cotto, who feared that the laws would be used to punish them for their reporting on public emergencies, especially reporting that reflects negatively on the government. “We celebrate this victory that protects two of our most fundamental rights: freedom of the press and freedom of expression,” said Fermín Arraiza-Navas, legal director of the ACLU of Puerto Rico. “This dangerous law, signed first by former Governor Ricardo Rosselló and amended by a decadent legislature with the approval of Governor Wanda Vázquez in La Fortaleza, had only one objective: to criminalize dissent and persecute the press in times of emergency simply for disagreeing with the official narrative. We will not allow it.” On March 31, 2023, the U.S. District Court for the District of Puerto Rico permanently enjoined the law, observing that the statute’s exceedingly broad sweep risked politicized prosecutions and chilling protected speech on matters of public concern. On August 4, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit affirmed, holding that the law violates the First Amendment because it imposes a content-based restriction on protected speech without adequate justification. The court noted that the law lacks essential limitations included in other false alarm statutes, and that it could be used to prosecute people who oppose the government’s views in debates about contentious issues such as the efficacy of masks during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as jokes, satire, or fiction. As the court wrote, Puerto Rico’s law “represents an impermissible restriction of speech, particularly during times of emergency when it is most imperative that the public be well-informed and the government held to account.” "With this law, the Government of Puerto Rico jeopardized the right to freedom of expression and freedom of the press, protections that are increasingly indispensable,” said Annette Martínez-Orabona, Executive Director of the ACLU of Puerto Rico. "This was also an attempt to discourage fair and necessary government oversight, precisely during emergencies like the one Puerto Rico is currently facing amid a drinking water service crisis. These rights are under attack on multiple fronts, and today we succeeded in protecting them." You can read the opinion here. You can read more about the law here. Court Case: Rodríguez-Cotto v. Press Release Aug 2026 Free Speech Professors Challenge Texas A&M System Over Censorship Policy, Detail Violations of Academic Freedom HOUSTON – A group of professors filed suit Monday night challenging the Texas A&M University System’s new censorship policy that prohibits faculty from discussing certain topics and viewpoints related to race, sexual orientation, and gender. “My ethics course — the only one of its kind available to graduate students — was canceled for noncompliance with a draconian censorship policy,” said Leonard Bright (he/him), lead plaintiff, professor of Public Service and Administration, and president of the Texas A&M College Station chapter of the AAUP. “This policy has impacted my ability to do my job, my students’ ability to learn, and my colleagues’ ability to teach without fear of reprisal. The chilling effect of this policy is vast and immeasurable, and it poisons the very soul of what a university should be: a place where ideas are free to roam, and debate is uninhibited by the political winds.” The policy, which was implemented in late 2025 and requires extensive, bureaucratic syllabi review, has resulted in prohibitions on everything from the Oscar-winning film “Moonlight” to Plato’s writings on gender. The faculty impacted by this policy work throughout the Texas A&M System, which includes 12 universities, and across departments, from the Bush School of Government and Public Service to the English department. “The First Amendment plainly prohibits this egregious attack on academic freedom at a public university,” said Emerson Sykes (he/him), senior staff attorney with the ACLU’s Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project. “This broad policy and the university’s opaque enforcement process makes it impossible to teach or to learn freely and endangers course content about everything from the history of slavery to Shakespeare to the hard sciences. Universities are sites of inquiry, debate, and discovery — banning entire categories of ideas is a betrayal of both their mission and the First Amendment.” The censorship policy was implemented in November 2025 amid a sustained campaign to limit speech on certain topics in the college classroom. As a result of the policy change, numerous classes have been cancelled or forced to remove content. The women’s and gender studies program has been shuttered altogether because the program could not be reconciled with the new censorship policy. “This policy directly harms Black, Brown, LGBTQIA+, and all other Texans who have historically been discriminated against by subjecting discussion of their rights, identities, and indeed very existence to heavy-handed censorship.” said Chloe Kempf (she/her), staff attorney at the ACLU of Texas. “What’s more, it undermines all Texans’ First Amendment rights. If public officials can abuse their power to ban these topics and perspectives today, there’s nothing stopping them from targeting other subjects and points of view, including your own, down the line.” Cancelled courses include Religions of the World; Introduction to Race and Ethnicity; Ethics in Public Policy; and a course focused on LGBTQ+ literature. Professors have been forced to edit their syllabi to comply with the policy, removing works like Plato’s “Myth of Androgyne;” Kevin Kruse’s “White Flight;” and even the Academy Award-winning film “Moonlight.” One history professor was allowed to teach Phyllis Schlafly’s campaign against the Equal Rights Amendment, but not about how the Fourteenth Amendment expanded to protect women and LGBTQ+ people. “By embarking on a campaign of censorship, Texas A&M has abdicated its responsibility to support students’ right to learn and faculty’s right to teach,” said Todd Wolfson (he/him), president of the AAUP. “A university that censors Plato — as well as other significant texts — abandons its obligation to truth, free inquiry, and the public trust.” The suit was filed on behalf of the American Association of University Professors (AAUP) and Professors Leonard Bright, Vanita Reddy, Landon Sadler, and Aaron George in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas. The complaint argues that the censorship policy governing Texas A&M is unconstitutionally vague and violates the First Amendment by discriminating against certain viewpoints. “We’re proud to represent these professors challenging a censorship policy that betrays Texas A&M’s established legacy as an institution that supports free and open inquiry,” said Jamie A. Aycock (he/him), attorney at Yetter Coleman LLP. “At stake in this lawsuit is the bedrock First Amendment principle that America is strengthened by and depends upon open public debate, even on the most controversial topics. Nowhere is this more important than in our public academic institutions, which are charged with developing and teaching our future leaders to think critically and broadly about pressing issues affecting society.” You can read the complaint here. title: Tenable Launches Industry’s First Open-Source AI Agent Exchange to Advance Collective Cyber Innovation and Defense
summary: CyberAgents Exchange powered by Tenable is an open-source AI hub powering collective cyber defense to discover, share and build trusted AI security components.
body_text: Tenable® Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: TENB), the exposure management company , today launched the CyberAgents Exchange , a new open-source AI exchange created to foster industry collaboration and improve collective cyber defense. The CyberAgents Exchange, powered by Tenable, is the only purpose-built, cybersecurity-native registry for AI agents, skills, MCP servers and multi-agent playbooks in the current market. Security teams are increasingly turning to AI to scale security operations and manage risk overload, but end up building AI agents in isolation, repeatedly reinventing the wheel. Existing AI exchanges are either general-purpose or vendor-gated, forcing security teams to wade through irrelevant use cases, waste time on duplicate design and build efforts, or accept restrictive vendor lock-in. To improve the cybersecurity industry’s collective defense and outpace AI-generated threats, defenders need a unified, cyber-specific hub to accelerate development and share collective agentic tooling. The CyberAgents Exchange eliminates these development silos and empowers industry collaboration with a truly open, free-to-use exchange. Built for trust and transparency, the Exchange provides code-level visibility into who built each AI component, when it was created and its peer-supported status. This transparency enables members to deploy AI components tailored to their specific organizational needs confidently. Additionally, the Exchange is a career asset for practitioners to build verifiable expertise in an emerging discipline and develop a catalog of peer-supported AI components. "The CyberAgents Exchange fills a major and pressing industry need, especially as cybersecurity remains a growing issue and AI-enabled attacks rise," said Seth Fogie, Director of Security for Baptist Memorial Health Care. "Its core philosophy of working together is what made the threat intelligence community so invaluable. My team has benefited greatly from the Exchange, and we look forward to contributing and collaborating with the wider community." Underscoring the industry’s commitment to collaborative, open-source AI defense, industry leaders SentinelOne and Recorded Future have joined the initiative as founding members of the CyberAgents Exchange. By contributing their deep expertise in autonomous security operations and threat intelligence, these industry pioneers will help anchor the Exchange as a truly unified, vendor-agnostic ecosystem. As founding members, both organizations will actively contribute secure AI agents, integration frameworks and playbooks to accelerate the community's defense capabilities against rapidly evolving AI-driven threats. In conjunction with the launch, Tenable is hosting “SWARM: The Cybersecurity Agentic AI Build Event,” a hands-on, multi-day event at Black Hat USA 2026 sponsored by AWS and presented with support from Anthropic. At the event, security practitioners will build open-source security agents, skill files or MCP servers. Winners will be announced on Thursday, August 6, 2026. More than 50 AI components, released under open-source licenses, are available, including: Navi (Agent): A command-line tool that leverages the Tenable One Vulnerability Management APIs to automate common vulnerability management and cyber exposure workflows. SentinelOne Purple AI (MCP Server): Allows users to access SentinelOne services with any MCP client. Recorded Future MITRE APT Attack Path Analysis (Skill): Pulls an organization’s Recorded Future threat map, maps an APT group's MITRE ATT&CK techniques and cross-references against live Tenable findings to identify which attack path nodes are actively exploitable. SOC-Hunter (Skill): Leveraged daily by Tenable’s internal security operations team, SOC-Hunter provides proactive, hypothesis-driven threat hunting using the LOCK pattern across SIEM, EDR, VM, CSPM, CASB and code search. The Hounds Pack (Playbook): A skill-packaged playbook for The Hounds — 18 exposure-management specialists that hunt, tag and calibrate risk. “Security is a team sport. We’ve addressed a gaping hole in the ecosystem of AI Agents, built for defenders, by defenders. With the CyberAgents Exchange, we’re creating a collaborative 'town square' where cybersecurity practitioners can build, test, improve and share the best in agentic defense,” said Vlad Korsunsky, Chief Technology Officer, Tenable. “With our deep roots in the open source community and our global ecosystem of customers and partners, Tenable is uniquely positioned to steward this collaborative effort to help scale security teams' capabilities and outpace evolving threats.” "To truly scale defenses against autonomous, AI-driven threats, the security community must move past isolated development and vendor-locked silos," said Braden Preston, vice president of product management, SentinelOne. "As a founding member of the CyberAgents Exchange, SentinelOne is proud to champion a transparent, open-source foundation for agentic security. By sharing trusted, autonomous components and collaborative playbooks, we are empowering security teams globally to innovate faster, defend smarter and outpace modern adversaries together." "Joining the CyberAgents Exchange as a founding member lets us bring world-class threat intelligence directly into the open-source frameworks security teams are building today," said Jamie Zajac, Chief Product Officer at Recorded Future. "But the promise of AI agents in security depends entirely on whether they can be trusted. Intelligence doesn't just make agents smarter. It makes them traceable, auditable and repeatable. That's the foundation the community needs to build autonomous defense that's not only fast, but reliable." The Tenable CyberAgents Exchange is a free, open-source community with no fees for listing or using agents. For more information and to contribute to the CyberAgents Exchange, please visit: exchange.tenable.com About Tenable Tenable® is the exposure management company, exposing and closing the cybersecurity gaps that erode business value, reputation and trust. The company’s AI-powered exposure management platform radically unifies security visibility, insight and action across the attack surface, equipping modern organizations to protect against attacks from IT infrastructure to cloud environments to critical infrastructure and everywhere in between. By protecting enterprises from security exposure, Tenable reduces business risk for over 40,000 customers around the globe. title: Spok-Powered Hospitals Recognized on 2026-2027 U.S. News & World Report's Best Hospitals Honor Roll
summary: Leading 2026-2027 Best Hospitals Honor Roll recipients are among the more than 2,000 hospitals worldwide that depend on Spok solutions to drive care coordination and deliver exceptional patient outcomes.
body_text: Leading healthcare systems continue to rely on Spok to drive care coordination and deliver exceptional patient outcomes. Plano, Texas. (Aug. 6, 2026) – Spok, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Spok Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: SPOK) and a global leader in healthcare communications, today reported that 18 of the 20 adult hospitals featured on the 2026-2027 U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals Honor Roll use Spok technology to enhance care coordination and support exceptional patient care. For over a decade, the majority of Honor Roll hospitals have consistently leveraged Spok solutions to streamline workflows and improve care team coordination. “We congratulate these Honor Roll hospitals on their outstanding achievement. Their recognition reflects years of dedication to patient care and clinical excellence,” said Vincent D. Kelly, chief executive officer of Spok Holdings, Inc. “We are grateful for the trust they place in Spok to strengthen communication across their care teams and remain committed to providing the communication infrastructure that helps their teams deliver outstanding care.” The 2026-2027 Honor Roll recipients are among the more than 2,000 hospitals worldwide that depend on Spok solutions to eliminate communication barriers, accelerate clinical response times, and enhance patient experiences. As the global authority on hospital rankings, the U.S. News & World Report has compiled the U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals Honor Roll for over three decades. This recognition program evaluates approximately 4,500 healthcare organizations annually, naming 20 of the country’s highest-performing hospitals among 14 adult specialties or specialty areas and 23 procedures and conditions. The rankings are extensively referenced because they prioritize measurable, data-driven indicators of hospital performance, including patient outcomes, nursing quality, and patient experience.

title: Phunware Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
body_text: Phunware Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Download as PDF August 06, 2026 4:05pm EDT Related Documents Revenue Increased 76% Year-Over-Year, Gross Margin Expanded to 69% Maintained $92 Million Cash Position with No Debt to Support Continued Product Innovation and Growth Appointed Chief Executive Officer and Senior Vice President of Sales and AI and Digital Transformation Veterans to Lead Company's Next Phase of Growth AUSTIN, Texas, Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phunware, Inc. (“Phunware” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PHUN), a mobile-first enterprise guest intelligence platform company delivering location-aware guest intelligence and AI-enabled guest engagement tools, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Financial Highlights Net revenue increased 76% to $0.8 million in the second quarter of 2026, compared to $0.5 million in the second quarter of 2025 as a result of a customer-initiated early contract termination. For the first six months of 2026, net revenue increased 17% to $1.3 million, compared to $1.1 million in the prior-year period. Gross margin improved to 69.0% in the second quarter of 2026 from 41.8% in the prior-year period and increased to 69.7% for the first six months of 2026 from 48.0% in the prior-year period. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $92.1 million as of June 30, 2026, with no debt, providing significant financial flexibility to execute the Company's growth strategy. Net loss was $5.2 million, or ($0.26) per basic and diluted share, in the second quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of $3.1 million, or ($0.16) per basic and diluted share, in the prior-year period. The increase primarily reflects continued investment in product, sales and marketing, research and development, and general and administrative initiatives supporting the Company's 2.0 Strategy. Net loss was $8.4 million, or ($0.42) per basic and diluted share, in the first six months of 2026, compared to a net loss of $6.9 million, or ($0.34) per basic and diluted share, in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $5.5 million in the second quarter of 2026, compared to an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $4.1 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.5 million in the first six months of 2026, compared to an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $8.9 million in the prior-year period. Net cash used in operations was $8.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to $6.8 million for the prior-year period. Recent Business Highlights Continued execution of the Company's 2.0 Strategy, unifying Phunware's mobile, location-aware, and AI capabilities into a single AI-enabled Guest Intelligence Platform designed for hospitality, healthcare, and other complex physical environments. Appointed Dmitry Kroshka as Chief Executive Officer, effective May 13, 2026, to lead execution of the Company's strategic transformation. Engaged Michael Cerdá and his AI-first product transformation firm, Build Something Product Group, to accelerate the Company's 2.0 product development and execution. Appointed hospitality technology veterans Nick Farrell and Brent McMahan as Senior Vice President of Sales and Senior Director of Sales, respectively, to expand the Company's hospitality business development efforts. Showcased the Company's expanding AI-enabled Guest Intelligence Platform at HITEC North America 2026, featuring live demonstrations of AI Concierge, the AI Itinerary Builder, and the forthcoming Location-Aware Data Layer. Appointed AI and technology veterans Aaron Holloway and Michael Crooks as advisors. Continued strong commercial momentum for AI Concierge and related guest engagement metrics following its launch in January 2026. Maintained running 12-month customer retention of greater than 95%. Management Commentary “Building on the strong momentum generated at the Hospitality Industry Technology Exposition and Conference (“HITEC”), where live demonstrations of Phunware's evolving Guest Intelligence Platform—including AI Concierge and AI Itinerary Builder—captured significant interest from hospitality professionals, the Company continues to advance its Product and Sales initiatives,” said Dmitry Kroshka, Chief Executive Officer of Phunware. “Since becoming Chief Executive Officer, my focus has been on translating our technology, expertise, customer relationships, and strong balance sheet into disciplined execution of our 2.0 Strategy. We believe this quarter marks an important milestone in Phunware's evolution. "We believe traditional hospitality technology helps operators understand who guests are and what they have done. Our vision is to deliver a platform which helps them understand what guests are doing in real time and enable them to engage and respond to guests while those interactions are occurring. By combining our mobile platform, proprietary location-aware technology, and AI capabilities into a unified Guest Intelligence Platform, we believe we can deliver a differentiated solution that originates and improves guest experiences while creating new opportunities for our customers to drive engagement, data collection, and on-property revenue. "During the second quarter, we continued to advance our product roadmap and strengthen our commercial organization. AI Concierge is now commercially deployed and generating engagement levels well above our initial expectations. At HITEC, we showcased the next phase of our platform with AI Itinerary Builder, which is designed to help operators personalize guest experiences and increase ancillary revenue opportunities, along with our forthcoming Location-Aware Data Layer, which is designed to connect digital guest interactions with real-world operational and revenue outcomes. We also strengthened our internal sales leadership team by hiring Nick Farrell as Senior Vice President of Sales, who will lead the Company’s hospitality growth strategy, and Brent McMahan as Senior Director of Sales, who brings more than a decade of experience in hospitality technology sales. Further, we engaged Michael Cerdá and Build Something Product Group to accelerate 2.0 Product development, and added advisors Aaron Holloway and Michael Crooks, both veterans in technology and AI. "We are executing the 2.0 strategy from a position of financial strength. We ended the quarter with approximately $92 million in cash and cash equivalents and no debt, providing flexibility to continue investing in product innovation, intellectual property, and strategic growth initiatives. While hospitality remains our primary commercial focus, we believe the same AI-enabled, location-aware intelligence platform can be applied to address meaningful opportunities across healthcare and other complex physical environments and intend to do so. We remain confident that our 2.0 strategy, product roadmap, and balance sheet best position the Company to create long-term value for shareholders. “To that end, I intend to lead a series of new investor relations initiatives designed to provide shareholders with a regular cadence of communication and transparency into our 2.0 Strategy, including investor webinars, regular updates on our progress, a comprehensive investor presentation, and an expanded presence at key investor and industry conferences. We look forward to keeping our shareholders informed and engaged as we continue to execute on our strategy,” concluded Kroshka.
