body_text: Having a baby is one of the biggest changes a person can experience. Parents are often told to enjoy every moment because babies grow up so quickly. However, the first few months can feel less like a beautiful, fast-moving experience and more like a constant cycle of feeding, changing, cleaning, appointments, worrying and trying to get enough sleep. For many new parents, the biggest challenge is time. There never seems to be enough of it. A day has only 24 hours, but suddenly almost every hour seems to belong to someone else. Research into parenthood and time management shows that finding balance is not simply about creating more free time. It is about learning how to use the time we already have in a healthier and more meaningful way. Here are five important lessons that can help new parents manage their time and adjust to life with a baby. 1. Learn to work with your baby's schedule One of the first things new parents discover is that babies do not always follow a planned schedule. Parents may want their baby to sleep, eat or wake up at particular times, but newborns have their own needs and rhythms. Trying to control every part of the baby's routine can create unnecessary stress. Instead, parents can learn to be flexible and respond to what their baby needs. This does not mean that routines are bad. A simple routine can make family life easier. The important thing is to avoid expecting everything to happen exactly according to plan. Parents can ask themselves whether they are trying to control time or simply trying to work with the people around them. Sometimes adjusting your expectations can make the day feel much easier. 2. Do not forget who you were before becoming a parent After having a baby, it is easy for your entire identity to become connected to being a mother or father. Feeding, cleaning, changing nappies and looking after the baby can take up so much time that personal interests and relationships are forgotten. However, keeping some connection with your old life can be good for your wellbeing. You might continue talking to friends, reading, exercising, listening to music, cooking, watching a favourite programme or spending time on a hobby. These activities do not have to take hours. Even small amounts of personal time can make a difference. Looking after yourself does not mean that you love your baby any less. In fact, having some time to recharge can help you become more patient and present with your family. If something is important to you, try to give it a small but regular place in your life. 3. Saving time does not always mean having more free time Parents who have more money may be able to pay for services such as childcare, cleaning, takeaway meals or other forms of help. These services can certainly reduce some of the pressure. But there is an important problem. When one task disappears, another task can quickly take its place. For example, a parent might save an hour by ordering food but then spend that hour answering work emails. Someone else might hire a cleaner but use the extra time to deal with other responsibilities. This means that creating free time is not enough. Parents also need to protect that free time. If you manage to create an extra hour, it does not always need to be used for work. You could sleep, eat properly, take a walk, talk to your partner or simply sit quietly. Health should also be treated as a priority. Skipping meals and constantly sacrificing sleep may seem necessary in the short term, but it can make life harder in the long term. 4. Accept help from other people Having a baby can sometimes be surprisingly lonely. Friends and relatives may visit to see the baby, but that does not necessarily mean the parents are receiving practical help. Sometimes people genuinely want to help but do not know what to do. New parents can be more specific. Instead of simply saying, "Thank you for visiting," they might ask a trusted visitor to hold the baby while they shower, prepare a meal, wash some dishes or go to the supermarket. Asking for help is not a sign of failure. Looking after a baby is difficult work, and having support can make a huge difference. Community is also important. Parks, libraries, community centres and parent groups can give new parents opportunities to meet other people and escape the feeling of being alone at home. Time becomes easier to manage when it is shared with people who care about you. 5. Give yourself time to feel New parenthood can bring many different emotions. There can be happiness, excitement, fear, frustration, exhaustion and uncertainty, sometimes all on the same day. But dealing with emotions takes time. When parents are constantly busy, they may not have enough space to think about how they actually feel. This can lead to emotional exhaustion. It is therefore important to protect small moments that are not about productivity. You might sit quietly with a cup of tea, take a short walk, talk honestly with your partner or spend a few minutes reflecting on your day. These moments may appear unimportant compared with feeding the baby or completing household tasks. However, emotional rest is also a form of self-care. Parents do not need to make every minute productive. Conclusion Having a baby can completely change the way a person experiences time. The solution is not always to find more hours in the day because nobody can create more than 24 hours. Instead, new parents can learn to use their existing time differently. They can work with their baby's natural rhythm instead of trying to control everything. They can protect small parts of their identity outside parenthood. They can make sure that time saved through paid help is actually used for rest. They can accept practical support from friends and family. Most importantly, they can give themselves enough quiet time to understand and experience their emotions. Time is often described as something that can be saved, spent or purchased. But for new parents, time is also how relationships are built and how love is experienced. The quiet moments with a baby, the conversations with family, the short breaks and even the seemingly unproductive hours can all have value. For new parents, finding balance does not mean doing everything perfectly. Sometimes it simply means accepting that some things can wait, asking for help when it is needed and making space for the moments that matter most.

body_text: You post a pair of sneakers online. Within minutes, the comments start rolling in. "UP." "LP?" "MOP?" "RFS?" If you're new to online selling in the Philippines, it can feel like everyone is speaking a different language. In a way, they are. Over the years, Filipino sellers have developed their own shorthand across Facebook Marketplace, buy-and-sell groups, Instagram, TikTok Shop, and live selling. Knowing what these terms mean helps you respond faster, avoid misunderstandings, and keep buyers from dropping off before they complete a purchase. This guide breaks down the online selling terms you'll see most often, starting with one of the most common. What Does "UP" Mean in Online Selling? Quick answer: In Philippine online selling, "UP" means "under post." It's a comment used to bump a listing higher in Facebook's feed. Every new comment signals activity, making the post more likely to appear in front of other buyers. Sellers use it to keep listings visible. Buyers use it to save a post they want to revisit later. Here's why it works. Facebook groups prioritize recent activity. As older posts get pushed down the feed, even a single comment can make a listing appear active again. Instead of creating a new post, sellers simply comment "UP" to bring it back into circulation. You'll also come across a few variations: UP — the standard bump. Pa-up / Up mo — asking someone to bump the post. UPP / UUP — the same thing, just with extra emphasis. Up for grabs — different meaning entirely. It simply means the item is still available. Why Buyers Comment "UP" It's not just sellers. Many buyers comment "UP" to keep track of a listing. Once they've commented, Facebook sends them notifications whenever the seller replies or updates the post, making it easy to check back without searching for it again. Some buyers also bump listings so friends or family can see them. How to Reply to "UP" Don't waste the opportunity with a simple "Thanks." Someone just helped put your listing back in front of more buyers. Use your reply to answer the questions people usually ask before they buy. “Thanks for the up! Still available. LP is ₱2,800. MOP: GCash, Maya, card, or bank transfer. Ships nationwide. You can pay here: [payment link]” In one reply, you've answered the three questions most buyers ask first and given them a way to check out immediately. The fewer messages buyers need to send before paying, the more likely they are to complete the purchase. Filipino Online Selling Terms, Explained Now that you know what UP means, here's a glossary of the abbreviations and slang you'll see every day, grouped by where they usually come up, from browsing listings to negotiating prices and getting paid. Buying and Browsing Terms TERM STANDS FOR WHAT IT MEANS LF Looking For Buyer is searching for a specific item. “LF: iPhone 13 128GB” ISO In Search Of Same as LF FS For Sale The item is being sold FT For Trade Seller wants to swap, not sell PO Pre-order Item isn't in hand yet; you pay now, receive later OH On Hand Item is physically with the seller, ready to ship HTF Hard To Find Rare item, usually priced accordingly PM Private Message “PM me” — take it to DMs OOS Out Of Stock Sold out UP Under Post Bumps the listing (see above) Item Condition Terms TERM STANDS FOR WHAT IT MEANS BNS Brand New Sealed Unopened, factory sealed BNIB Brand New In Box New, box opened but unused BNWT Brand New With Tags Clothing, tags still attached NBU Never Been Used Owned but unused DOP Date Of Purchase When the seller originally bought it — matters for warranty RFS Reason For Selling Why they're letting it go. Buyers ask this to sniff out defects WW When Worn Photo of the item actually being worn, not flat-lay DEFECT — Seller is disclosing damage. Always ask for photos STEAL — Priced well below market. “Steal price!” Price and Negotiation Terms TERM STANDS FOR WHAT IT MEANS LP Lowest Price “LP?” = what's the least you'll take? SRP Suggested Retail Price Original store price, used to show the discount DP Down Payment Partial payment to reserve an item NP Negotiable Price Seller is open to offers FIRM — Price is not negotiable RESERVED — Someone has claimed it, pending payment Payment and Delivery Terms This is the group that decides whether you actually get your money. TERM STANDS FOR WHAT IT MEANS MOP Mode Of Payment How the buyer will pay — GCash, bank transfer, card, COD MOD Mode Of Delivery How it ships — Lalamove, J&T, Grab, meetup COD Cash On Delivery Buyer pays the courier on arrival SF Shipping Fee Delivery cost, usually on the buyer PAYO Pay All Your Own Group buys — each buyer covers their own shipping MU Meet Up Hand-to-hand transaction OTW On The Way Item has shipped / seller is en route FULL Full Payment Total amount, no installment Live Selling Terms Live selling on Facebook and TikTok moves fast and has its own vocabulary. TERM STANDS FOR WHAT IT MEANS MINE — Claims the item. First “mine” usually wins FF Fast Fingers First to comment gets it. No reservations CF Confirm Seller confirming your claim went through PAID — Buyer announcing payment sent CO Check Out Buyer is ready to pay and close the order SOLD — Item is gone MOP Is the Term That Decides Whether You Get Paid Scroll through any buy-and-sell group and you'll see the same question again and again: "MOP?" It stands for Method of Payment. By the time a buyer asks, they've usually decided they want the item. They're asking how to pay. This is where many online sellers lose the sale. The typical reply looks something like this: a GCash number, a bank account, instructions to send a screenshot, then a wait while the seller checks if the payment arrived. It works. Until you're handling dozens of orders. Every extra message slows the checkout. Every extra step gives buyers another chance to change their mind. There's also the trust problem. Sending money to a stranger's personal account isn't something every buyer is comfortable with. Many would rather buy from someone who offers a proper checkout. A checkout page removes the back and forth. The buyer opens a link, chooses GCash, Maya, cards, QR Ph, or online banking, and pays. You receive the payment automatically. No screenshots to verify, no receipts to match. How to Accept Different Payment Methods The best way to collect payments depends on how you sell. If you're on social media, you don't even need a website. Selling in Facebook comments or DMs? Use Payment Links. Selling one item at a time? Create a payment link for the exact amount and send it in the conversation. When someone comments "Mine" or asks "MOP?" , reply with the link instead of your personal account details. The buyer pays using GCash, Maya, cards, QR Ph, or online banking, and you're notified as soon as the payment goes through. It's the fastest option for one-off sales, Facebook Marketplace listings, and live selling. Create a Payment Link Selling from your bio or product catalog? Use Payment Pages. If you regularly sell multiple products, share one permanent payment page instead. Add it to your Instagram or TikTok bio, pin it on Facebook, or include it in your posts. Buyers can browse your products and check out on their own. No website required. Create a Payment Page Already have a website? Use Hosted Checkout. If you sell through your own website, redirect buyers to a PayMongo-hosted checkout instead of building your own payment form. You can accept GCash, Maya, cards, QR Ph, and other payment methods while PayMongo securely handles the payment flow and PCI-DSS compliance. Explore Hosted Checkout Using Shopify, WooCommerce, or Wix? Install a plugin. If your store already runs on an ecommerce platform, install a PayMongo plugin to add GCash, Maya, cards, and QR Ph to your existing checkout. No custom integration required. Get PayMongo Plugin Which One Should You Start With? YOU SELL MAINLY THROUGH USE THIS Facebook group comments, DMs, live selling Payment Links Instagram / TikTok bio, a shareable catalog Payment Pages Your own custom website Hosted Checkout Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix Plugins Most sellers start with payment links, then add a payment page once they're posting inventory regularly. Stop Losing Sales at “MOP?” You sourced the item, shot the photos, wrote the caption, and answered the comments. Losing the buyer at the payment step is an expensive way to end that. Accept GCash, Maya, cards, QR Ph, and online banking – no setup fee, no monthly fee. You only pay when you get paid. Create a Free Account Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between LP and SRP? LP is Lowest Price — the least the seller will accept, usually asked by buyers negotiating. SRP is Suggested Retail Price, the original store price, which sellers quote to show how big a discount they're offering. What does RFS mean and why do buyers ask it? RFS means Reason For Selling. Buyers ask because the answer often reveals problems — a phone sold because of battery issues, or shoes sold because they don't fit. A vague RFS is a common warning sign in secondhand deals. Do I need a website to accept online payments in the Philippines? No. With PayMongo payment links you can send a checkout link straight into a Facebook comment, DM, or Viber chat. If you want a shareable catalog instead, a payment page gives you a storefront-style link with no website required. Is it safe to accept payments through a payment link? Payment links route buyers to a secure, PCI-DSS compliant checkout rather than asking them to send money to a personal account. That protects you from receipt-editing scams and gives buyers a reason to trust a seller they've never met.

title: Shopify Singapore: A guide for businesses and online sellers in 2026
summary: Learn how to start a Shopify store in Singapore. Compare pricing plans, payment gateways e.g. HitPay and Stripe, GST rules, ACRA requirements, and tips for 2026
body_text: What is Shopify and why Singapore businesses choose it Shopify is a hosted e-commerce platform that lets you build and run an online store. According to Shoprank, 37.7% of all Singapore e-commerce stores use Shopify as their platform. The advantages are clear – no managing servers, security updates, or PCI compliance. While that saves time, it's not the main reason businesses around the world choose Shopify. The key benefit here is control. Unlike e-commerce platforms like Shopee and Lazada, Shopify allows merchants to be in charge of their brands, customer information, and checkouts. You will be able to create an email list, implement loyalty programs, and sell directly to your clients. You can even control your own audience with Shopify. Founder Tip: If your product is a common everyday product (think, phone cases) and you're optimising for discovery, a marketplace-first strategy with a lean Shopify store often outperforms an all-in Shopify launch. Where Shopify suits Singapore-based founders Cross-border ready: Shopify supports multi-currency pricing, localised checkout, and Shopify Markets, making it easier for e-commerce stores to expand into nearby markets like Malaysia, Indonesia, and Australia. Strong app ecosystem: Founders can add battle-tested apps for subscriptions, loyalty, customer support, and accounting without having to write code on their own. Flexible payments: Shopify supports multiple payment providers, giving Shopify businesses in Singapore more options beyond a single processor. Why Shopify is growing in Singapore Three forces are pushing more Singapore founders onto Shopify as compared to other marketplaces or website builders. 1. Cross-border demand is now the default Singapore's small domestic market means most ecommerce brands here are cross-border by necessity. Many sell into Malaysia and Indonesia via Shopify Markets, fulfill orders from Australian customers, or source from China. 2. Omnichannel expectations have caught up with small and medium-sized enterprise budgets Shopify POS now makes it realistic for a founder running a pop-up at a market or a physical retail counter to sync inventory with the online store without a separate system. In fact, according to the same Shoprank research, 52% of all Shopify stores in Singapore have a physical distribution store. 3. DTC economics reward owned infrastructure DTC (Direct-to-consumer) is a business model where brands sell directly to customers through their own website instead of relying on third-party marketplaces or retailers. Paid social advertising is getting more expensive. To survive, brands need to own their customer relationship: email retargeting, post-purchase flows, loyalty programs. None of that works if you're just a listing on someone else's marketplace. You need your own checkout. Many Shopify stores today are launched by sellers who first proved demand on Shopee or Lazada. They now use Shopify to build a brand, own customer relationships, and reduce marketplace commissions. Shopify pricing in Singapore Shopify's core subscription plans are billed in USD globally, and Singapore is no exception for the three main tiers; only the entry-level Starter plan is currently shown to Singapore visitors in SGD $7/month. [Table:1] How to set up Shopify in Singapore Shopify's own onboarding is very intuitive and friendly. It's the order of decisions that actually matters, because doing them out of sequence is the single biggest source of relaunch rework. Register a business: You can create a Shopify account before registering the business with ACRA. However, you need to register a business first to get a business bank account, integrate payment gateways, and issue invoices that comply with GST rules. Choose a Shopify plan: For most new businesses, the Basic plan should be sufficient at the beginning. Later, you can upgrade to other plans. Choose a suitable theme: It is recommended that you choose a theme according to your catalogue size and requirements rather than its design. Organise your products: Organise your products, collections, variants, and tags properly since this will save you a lot of time. Configure shipping first: Configure shipping zones and rates prior to enabling payments as the cost of shipping will determine your pricing strategy. Configure taxes: Keep GST off until your business becomes GST-registered . Connect your domain: Connect your domain using a Shopify domain name or DNS. Enable payments: Enable Shopify Payments (if available), local payments such as PayNow or GrabPay. Test your store: Test your store by placing a test order, processing a refund, and testing the shipping, tax, and checkout configuration. Track your performance from the start: Set up analytics before running any product or store launch. Launch checklist [Table:2] Shopify Seller Center and Shopify Login for Singapore businesses If you're setting up your first Shopify store in Singapore, one of the first things you'll notice is that there's no separate Shopify Seller Center like on Shopee or Lazada. That often catches first-time founders off guard. Instead, Shopify gives every merchant a single Shopify Admin dashboard where you manage your entire business. After creating your store, you'll use your Shopify login (sometimes searched as seller Shopify login) to access everything. This includes from adding products and processing orders to configuring payment gateways and tracking sales. Whether you're searching for Shopify Seller Center, or Shopify login, they all lead to the same place: your Shopify Admin dashboard. From your dashboard, you can: Add and manage products Process and fulfill customer orders Configure shipping and tax settings Connect payment providers such as Shopify Payments, HitPay, or Stripe Install apps from the Shopify App Store Monitor sales, traffic, and customer insights Founder tip: Bookmark your Shopify Admin login page once your store is set up. Many first-time founders end up searching for "Shopify login" every time they want to access their store, but saving the direct login page makes it quicker. Payment gateways for Shopify stores in Singapore Shopify Payments covers cards and several accelerated checkout methods, but many Singapore merchants still choose another gateway such as HitPay to offer PayNow and additional local payment options. [Table:3] Decision matrix Selling mainly in Singapore? Use Shopify Payments + HitPay to support credit cards, PayNow, and the payment methods most local shoppers prefer. Selling internationally? Consider gateways that support multi-currency settlement or local payout currencies to reduce foreign exchange costs. Shopify Payments Advanced now supports multi-currency payouts too. Selling higher-value products? Add Atome or GrabPay PayLater to improve conversion rates for categories like fashion, beauty, and electronics. Common mistake: Relying only on Shopify Payments because it's the easiest option. Many Singapore shoppers expect PayNow at checkout. If you only accept cards, you may create unnecessary friction and lose conversions. Add local payment methods early and test your checkout experience before scaling traffic. GST and compliance for Shopify sellers in Singapore Singapore's GST rate is currently 9%, effective from 1 January 2024, and the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) confirms no rate change for 2026. GST registration becomes compulsory once your taxable turnover exceeds SGD $1 million over a 12-month period. If you're below that threshold, you can register voluntarily, but for most new stores, the extra compliance isn't worth it. What this means practically for a new Shopify founder: Only charge GST if you're registered or legally required to register: Most new Shopify stores should keep GST turned off until they're required or choose to register voluntarily. Monitor your turnover: If you're approaching SGD $1 million in taxable turnover, review it regularly to avoid late GST registration. Know the OVR rules: Overseas businesses selling digital services or low-value goods into Singapore may be subject to the Overseas Vendor Registration (OVR) regime. Plan for e-invoicing: InvoiceNow is being rolled out in phases for GST-registered businesses, so planning for compatibility early can reduce future compliance work. Founder tip: In Singapore, cards remain popular, but PayNow and GrabPay are now mainstream checkout options. Supporting local payment methods can reduce checkout friction. Register Your Business with ACRA If your business is profit-based, then ACRA registration is mandatory, regardless of whether your business is an online shop or not. A sole proprietorship registration process is fast, whereas a Pte Ltd structure is ideal for scaling and financing. Comply with the requirements of the PDPA Act If you are gathering personal customer data like names, emails, and order history, then you must ensure that you have privacy policies in place and have the customer's consent. Shopify apps every Singapore merchant should consider [Table:4] Ten mistakes Singapore founders make on Shopify It is relatively easy to establish a Shopify store in Singapore. However, even minor setup errors will affect payments, taxation, cost, and customer experience. Here are some of the most frequent mistakes you should avoid when setting up your ecommerce store. Relying only on Shopify Payments: Add a PayNow-enabled gateway like HitPay before launch to support local payment preferences. Enabling GST too early: Keep GST disabled until you're registered, and monitor your turnover as you approach the registration threshold. ACRA registration timing: Register your business after commencing business operations to make banking and payment gateway approval easier. Choosing a theme solely based on aesthetics : Choose a theme which is suitable to your catalogue size and features and not only how it looks. Installing multiple applications: Begin with core applications and install others only if they meet your operational needs. Not checking FX charges: If you pay for your goods/services in foreign currency, always check FX rates. When your sales rise, FX charges can add up and eat into your profits. Enabling all Shopify Markets simultaneously: Begin with Singapore and then move on to other markets. Underestimating delivery costs: Ensure that you know how much it will cost you to send your goods using courier services before setting shipping rates. Budgeting only for the Shopify subscription fee: Ensure that you budget for app subscriptions, themes, transaction fees, and development costs. Failing to conduct a test order: Carry out a test order and refund before you launch your store. Optimising your Shopify store for growth Once your store is live, the next priority is attracting qualified traffic and converting more visitors into customers. 1. Optimise for local search Use relevant keywords in your page titles, meta descriptions, product descriptions, and image alt text. If you're targeting Singapore customers, naturally include local keywords where appropriate. 2. Improve your storefront High-quality product images, clear product descriptions, customer reviews, and a fast, mobile-friendly checkout can all help improve conversion rates. Make it as friction-less and appealing as you can. 3. Track what matters Connect Google Analytics and Google Search Console to monitor traffic, identify your best-performing pages, and find opportunities to improve your store over time. Keep a look at what your competitors are doing, and fix your strategy accordingly Managing your finances as your Shopify business grows As your business grows, you'll need to handle a lot of expenses. You will have to pay suppliers, track SaaS subscriptions, handle accounting, and also manage multiple currencies. For people just starting out with Shopify, it is easy for your business finances to end up spread across multiple banks, and spreadsheets. Aspire brings these financial workflows together in one place. You can hold and manage multiple currencies, pay overseas suppliers, issue virtual corporate cards, and track expenses for your business, all from a single platform. Ready to devote more time growing your Shopify store? See how Aspire helps ecommerce businesses handle payments, expenses, and cash flow. Frequently asked questions Do I have to be ACRA registered to sell on Shopify? If you're carrying on the activity for profit on a continuing basis regularly buying stock to resell, taking orders as a business, yes, regardless of whether you're "just testing" or running it solo from home. There's no online-only exemption. Can I accept PayNow on my Shopify store? Yes, but not through Shopify Payments directly. You'll need a gateway like HitPay that integrates PayNow into Shopify's checkout, typically via a free plugin from the Shopify App Store. Which Shopify plan is best for a Singapore founder? Basic, for the large majority of new stores. Upgrade to Grow once your monthly sales volume is high enough so that the lower transaction-fee percentage saves you more than the extra subscription cost. Can I sell internationally from a Shopify store in Singapore? Yes. Shopify supports international selling through features such as Shopify Markets, multi-currency pricing, localised domains, and integrations with international shipping providers. Many Singapore businesses start by selling locally before expanding into nearby markets like Malaysia, Indonesia, and Australia. Do I need a business bank account for Shopify in Singapore? While you can create a Shopify store without one, a business bank account is generally required to receive payouts from payment gateways, separate business and personal finances, and simplify bookkeeping. If you've registered your business with ACRA, opening a dedicated business account is recommended before you start accepting orders. Can I connect my Shopify store to Shopee or Lazada? Yes. Many Singapore merchants sell on Shopify alongside marketplaces like Shopee and Lazada. Inventory management apps and omnichannel tools can sync products, inventory levels, and orders across multiple sales channels, reducing manual work and helping prevent overselling. How much does it cost to start a Shopify store in Singapore? For most new businesses, expect costs beyond just the Shopify subscription. In addition to your monthly plan, you may pay for a domain name, premium themes, paid apps, payment processing fees, marketing, and shipping. Starting lean with the Basic plan and only adding paid tools when needed is usually the most cost-effective approach. Is Shopify a better choice than Shopee or Lazada? It depends on your goals. Marketplaces like Shopee and Lazada are excellent for reaching existing shoppers quickly, while Shopify gives you full control over your brand, customer relationships, pricing, and checkout experience. Many successful Singapore businesses use both: marketplaces to acquire customers and Shopify to build a long-term, independent brand.

body_text: View All News Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Updates August 6, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Following U.S. regulatory discussions, accelerated approval strategy remains intact, supported by DENALI Part 2 Enrollment completed in Part 2a and 2b of the DENALI trial; Part 2c is enrolling DENALI Part 2 topline readout expected in 1H 2027 to allow for data maturation post full enrollment $174.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, providing runway into late 2027 to support execution of key milestones SAN DIEGO, Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zentalis® Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZNTL), a clinical oncology innovator advancing late-stage development of an investigational, potentially first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor, azenosertib, as a biomarker-driven treatment approach for ovarian cancer, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and highlighted recent corporate, regulatory and clinical progress and upcoming expected milestones. "We have achieved important milestones on the continued advancement of azenosertib in our registration-intended DENALI Phase 2 and ASPENOVA Phase 3 trials for patients with Cyclin E1-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), including completing the enrollment of DENALI Part 2b and aligning with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) following a Type D meeting on our selected dose and DENALI study population to support potential accelerated approval,” said Julie Eastland, Chief Executive Officer of Zentalis. "We remain as confident as ever that azenosertib has the potential to be an important oral, non-chemotherapy treatment option for the approximately 50% of PROC patients with Cyclin E1-positive tumors, who have limited options. We expect to provide the topline readout of DENALI Part 2 in 1H 2027. We continue to advance the confirmatory ASPENOVA Phase 3 trial with the goal of bringing a potential first-in-class WEE1 therapy to market for this underserved patient population globally. In addition to the lead indication, we see opportunity for expansion of azenosertib into platinum-sensitive settings of ovarian cancer and additional tumor types through combinations." "We are well capitalized as of June 30, 2026 with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $174.6 million to support the execution of key milestones and to continue advancing our regulatory strategy for both accelerated and full approval in PROC,” Ms. Eastland continued. Business Updates Regulatory Update: Met with the FDA in a Type D meeting regarding the Company’s accelerated approval strategy, including dose. The FDA had no objection to the continued study of the selected monotherapy dose of azenosertib at the 400mg once daily on a 5-days-on, 2-days-off schedule (400mg QD 5:2) in patients with Cyclin E1-positive PROC, selected based on a pre-specified interim analysis from DENALI Part 2a. The FDA acknowledged the DENALI Part 2 study population, including the 2c cohort, has the potential to support an accelerated approval pathway, subject to the strength of the data and the landscape of approved agents at the time of regulatory action. DENALI Part 2 Enrollment and Integrated Topline Readout: Enrollment in DENALI Parts 2a and 2b is complete. Earlier this year, the Company expanded DENALI Part 2 to broaden the overall study population and enrich patients previously treated with a taxane-containing regimen for PROC, aligning the study population with the evolving treatment landscape of approved agents. DENALI Part 2c is currently enrolling. The integrated dataset of DENALI Parts 2a, 2b, and 2c is designed to support accelerated approval in the Cyclin E1 biomarker-selected patient population, subject to regulatory review. The Company expects to provide a topline readout in 1H 2027 to allow for data maturation post full enrollment. ASPENOVA Phase 3 First Patient Dosed: In May 2026, announced the first patient was dosed in the Phase 3 ASPENOVA confirmatory trial designed to satisfy FDA requirements for U.S. full approval and to support approval in major ex-U.S. markets. The trial is currently enrolling. ESMO 2026 Abstract Acceptances: Announced that the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) has accepted an abstract for rapid oral presentation at the 2026 ESMO Annual Meeting featuring overall survival analysis from Part 1b of the DENALI study of azenosertib in PROC patients. A second abstract featuring the ASPENOVA Phase 3 trial design has been accepted for a trial-in-progress poster presentation. MUIR Clinical Trial Data Presented at ASCO 2026: Presented results from Part 1 of the Phase 1b MUIR trial at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, focusing on an evaluation of azenosertib in combination with paclitaxel in PROC. The data showed combinability and activity of azenosertib in an all-comer PROC setting, demonstrating the potential for azenosertib in multiple lines of ovarian cancer and more broadly in combination with cytotoxic agents in other tumor types. Part 2 enrollment is ongoing for azenosertib in combination with bevacizumab for 2L platinum sensitive ovarian cancer. Expanded Commercial Capabilities: In May 2026, announced the appointments of Shannon Campbell to the Company’s Board of Directors and Sarah Kelly as SVP of Commercial Strategy to support commercialization readiness. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $174.6 million as of June 30, 2026, compared to $245.9 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company believes that its existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026 will be sufficient to fund its operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into late 2027. Research and Development Expenses: Research and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $35.2 million, compared to $27.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase of $7.6 million was primarily due to a $7.0 million milestone payment to Recurium IP Holdings, LLC required as a result of the commencement of the Phase 3 ASPENOVA clinical trial and an increase of $5.2 million related to clinical expenses and drug manufacturing, including costs associated with advancing the DENALI and ASPENOVA trials. This increase was partially offset by a decrease of $4.5 million for personnel expense, of which $2.1 million was non-cash stock-based compensation, and a decrease of $0.1 million related to allocated overhead. General and Administrative Expenses: General and administrative expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $9.2 million, compared to $8.4 million during the three months ended June 30, 2025. This increase of $0.8 million was primarily attributable to an increase of $1.7 million for consulting and outside services. This increase was partially offset by a decrease of $0.9 million for non-cash stock-based compensation. Total Operating Expenses: Total operating expenses were $44.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $36.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. About Azenosertib Azenosertib is an investigational, potentially first-in-class, selective, and orally bioavailable inhibitor of WEE1 currently being evaluated in clinical studies in ovarian cancer and additional tumor types. WEE1 acts as a master regulator of the G1-S and G2-M cell cycle checkpoints, through negative regulation of both CDK1 and CDK2, to prevent replication of cells with damaged DNA. By inhibiting WEE1, azenosertib enables cell cycle progression, despite high levels of DNA damage, thereby resulting in the accumulation of DNA damage and leading to mitotic catastrophe and cancer cell death. Azenosertib is in late-stage development as a potential treatment for Cyclin E1-positive PROC. There is currently no approved treatment option specifically for this biomarker-selected population which comprises approximately 50% of PROC patients. Cyclin E1 protein overexpression has been established as a sensitive and specific predictive biomarker for identifying patients who could potentially derive benefit from azenosertib treatment. About DENALI Clinical Trial DENALI is a multi-part Phase 2 registration-intended clinical trial (NCT05128825) studying azenosertib in PROC patients. Part 1b enrolled patients with PROC regardless of Cyclin E1 protein expression, all treated at 400mg QD 5:2. Part 2 is prospectively enrolling PROC patients with Cyclin E1 protein overexpression based on Zentalis' proprietary immunohistochemistry cutoff. Part 2, in total, is designed to support accelerated approval, pending positive study outcomes and further discussions with the FDA. The study design consists of the following parts: Part 2a: Dose confirmation evaluated two doses, 300mg QD 5:2 and 400mg QD 5:2, with approximately 30 patients enrolled per dose group. 400mg QD 5:2 was selected as the optimal monotherapy dose. Recruitment at the 300mg QD 5:2 dose level has been discontinued. All patients enrolled in Part 2a will contribute to the overall safety database submitted to the FDA. Part 2b: Enrollment expansion at the selected 400mg QD 5:2 dose up to approximately 100 patients, including patients at this dose in Part 2a. This cohort has completed enrollment. Part 2c: Broadening study population, which is expected to include approximately 40 patients previously treated with a taxane-containing regimen for PROC. This cohort is currently enrolling. Zentalis expects to complete enrollment in all cohorts of DENALI Part 2 (2a, 2b, 2c) and provide a topline readout by 1H 2027. For physician and patient information about the DENALI trial, please visit www.denalitrial.com . About ASPENOVA Clinical Trial ASPENOVA is a Phase 3 randomized, confirmatory clinical trial designed to support full approval of azenosertib in patients with Cyclin E1-positive PROC. The trial is expected to enroll approximately 420 patients and compare azenosertib monotherapy at 400mg QD 5:2 to investigator's choice of standard-of-care single-agent chemotherapy (paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin [PLD], gemcitabine, or topotecan) in this biomarker-selected population. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS); key secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS) and overall response rate (ORR). The trial design was based on feedback from the U.S. FDA regarding requirements for seeking approval under the accelerated approval pathway and requirements to support potential conversion to full approval. About MUIR Clinical Trial MUIR (NCT04516447) is a multi-part, open-label Phase 1b clinical trial evaluating the safety, efficacy, and preliminary clinical activity of azenosertib combinations in patients with ovarian cancer. Part 1 enrolled patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) treated with azenosertib in combination with one of four chemotherapy regimens: carboplatin, gemcitabine, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or paclitaxel. Primary objectives are safety and tolerability, with key secondary objectives including clinical activity assessed by objective response rate, duration of response, and progression-free survival per RECIST v1.1. Part 2 is evaluating azenosertib plus bevacizumab as maintenance regimen (first [1L] or second line [2L]) in patients with advanced ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer following platinum-based chemotherapy. The dose expansion portion will evaluate azenosertib at the recommended dose in combination with bevacizumab in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in 2L who progressed while on a PARP inhibitor for 1L maintenance. The primary objective is safety and tolerability; secondary objectives include preliminary clinical activity of the combination as assessed by progression-free survival for the dose expansion portion. The dose expansion portion is currently open for enrollment. About Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Zentalis is a clinical oncology innovator developing a treatment approach for ovarian cancer and multiple tumor types. Leveraging therapeutics development and biomarker expertise, Zentalis is advancing monotherapy and combination studies of its investigational first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor, azenosertib. Focused on translating WEE1 science into clinical practice, we aim to equip physicians with a targeted, non-chemo, orally available medicine that enhances treatment experience, choice, and outcomes. Our mission: to unburden cancer patients with more convenience and care.​ For more information, please visit www.zentalis.com . Follow Zentalis on LinkedIn at www.linkedin.com/company/zentalis-pharmaceuticals . title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports up to 10,000 collections per collection group
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports up to 10,000 collections per collection group
body_text: The next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports up to 10,000 collections within a single collection group, increased from the previous limit of 1,500. Collection groups organize multiple collections and enable them to share OpenSearch Compute Units (OCUs), even when the collections are encrypted with different AWS KMS keys. With this higher limit, you can consolidate significantly more collections into a single collection group and manage them under a shared set of capacity limits. Customers use collection groups to reduce costs by sharing compute across many collections rather than provisioning separate OCUs for each KMS key, while still maintaining collection-level security and access controls. As customer workloads have grown, particularly for multi-tenant applications that provision a collection per tenant, the previous limit of 1,500 collections per group constrained how many tenants could benefit from a shared compute pool. Raising the limit to 10,000 collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless lets you scale these workloads further, improve compute utilization, and lower per-collection cost, without creating and operating additional collection groups. The higher limit applies automatically to new and existing nextgen collection groups. The increased limit is available on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless in all AWS Regions where it is available . To learn more, see Amazon OpenSearch Serverless technical documentation and quotas .

title: Your Company Is Racing to Deploy AI. Is Your Data Ready?
summary: Dataverse gives administrators practical controls for capacity, retention, security, auditing, and recovery.
body_text: AI increases the volume, value, and use of business data. Dataverse gives administrators practical controls for capacity, retention, security, auditing, and recovery. AI changes how business data is used Consider a manufacturer using AI in procurement, finance, and supply chain operations. A procurement leader wants agents to reconcile invoices, flag supplier exceptions, and update case records without adding manual review to every transaction. A platform administrator must support growth in transaction volume and data while keeping storage within entitlement, limiting each agent to the records and actions it needs, and preserving evidence of material changes. The administrator needs to answer practical questions each week. Which environments and tables are growing? Which records still support an active process? Which records must be retained for audit or regulatory review? Which users and agents can read or update them? Can the team recover a deleted record and explain who changed it? AI increases the frequency of these decisions because automated processes can read and change business data continuously. The governance job is to keep the data useful for the business process while managing capacity, access, retention, recovery, and evidence. AI raises the cost of poor data hygiene. Old, inactive, inaccurate, or incomplete records may once have sat unused and created only storage cost. When agents can retrieve that data, use it to answer questions, and take action, its quality can affect the result. Administrators need to govern how much data is retained and whether it is accurate, relevant, and appropriate for agentic use. Data growth requires clear ownership and policy Across industries, data administrators share a common set of operating needs: Data ownership. Connect each data set to an owner and a defined business purpose. Access model. Define which users and agents should be able to view or change the data. Lifecycle model. Decide whether data should remain active, move to long-term retention, or be deleted on a schedule. Review schedule. Revisit the policy regularly to confirm the data, access model, and lifecycle treatment still support the business process. These needs take different forms across industries. Healthcare: A records administrator must keep clinical records available for care, legal holds, and required retention periods while identifying older, inactive records that no longer need to remain in active storage. The job is to reduce active storage use without weakening access controls or record availability. Retail: A commerce platform owner must absorb seasonal growth in orders, service cases, files, logs, and agent interactions. The job is to identify which data still supports returns, service, fraud review, or analytics, then apply retention and deletion policies by record type rather than carrying every seasonal peak forward. Financial services: A security or compliance lead must approve how an agent accesses customer and transaction records. The job is to grant the minimum required privileges, record consequential changes, and produce evidence for internal review or audit. Manufacturing: A platform administrator must manage the records generated by procurement and supply chain agents. The job is to trace capacity growth to specific environments and tables, assign a business owner, retain records required for supplier or financial review, and recover records deleted by a person or automated process. Dataverse capabilities for data governance Dataverse provides governance controls that prepare business data for agentic access, including storage management, access controls, audit history, lifecycle management for inactive and deleted data, and environment governance. The following actions provide a practical starting point for organizations expanding AI use across business applications. See what is driving storage. In the Power Platform admin center, review tenant and environment usage across database, file, and log capacity, then drill into the environments and tables consuming the most storage. Review Dataverse capacity reporting . Retain inactive data without keeping it active. Create Dataverse long-term retention policies for eligible table records that must remain available for audit, legal, regulatory, or limited inquiry purposes. Retained data stays secured by Dataverse and becomes read-only. Understand long-term retention and set a retention policy . Create a recovery window before deleting data. Administrators can enable deleted-record keeping for 1 to 30 days and restore supported records deleted manually, automatically, singly, or in bulk. Use this as a safety net for lifecycle actions: establish that data is inactive or safe to delete, validate scope and dependencies, and configure recovery before acting. Configure and use deleted-record recovery . Constrain who can see and change business data. Dataverse security roles define access to apps, tables, records, and data operations; roles can be scoped through access levels, teams, and business units. Review security roles and privileges . Preserve evidence of consequential changes. Dataverse auditing can record the creation of records, updates, deletes, sharing changes, security-role changes, and user access when configured. Audit data consumes log capacity, so audit scope and retention should be deliberate. Configure Dataverse auditing . Apply supported governance rules across environments. Power Platform environment groups let administrators apply available managed governance rules across selected managed environments, including documented security, sharing, AI, backup-retention, and application-lifecycle settings. Not every Dataverse data-governance control is available as an environment-group rule, so verify the current rule catalog before defining centralized policy. Explore managed governance . Administrators must configure these controls and align them with business, legal, security, and records-management requirements. Audit scope affects log capacity. Retention and deletion policies require clear record ownership. Security roles require periodic review as applications and automated processes change. Establish clear accountability for data governance Use a shared operating model: platform administrators should define and enforce the governance process, while business owners classify data and select the correct policy. Platform administrators should define policy by record type and intended use, configure available controls, review the organization’s posture on a regular schedule, and address exceptions or unusual growth. Business owners should identify the purpose, sensitivity, operational value, and retention requirements of records. Security, compliance, legal, and records-management teams should define additional access, evidence, and retention requirements. This operating model combines human decisions with product configuration. Dataverse can enforce configured access, auditing, retention, recovery, and environment settings; the organization remains responsible for classifying data, selecting the correct policy, reviewing exceptions, and confirming that controls meet business and regulatory needs. Use Dataverse as the governed business data layer Dataverse applies storage reporting, lifecycle controls, role-based security, auditing, and recovery to the business records used by applications and automated processes. This provides a consistent control model for data stored in Dataverse. Administrators use the Power Platform admin center to manage environments, capacity, security settings, auditing, and deleted-record recovery. Makers configure table-level retention policies in Power Apps. Organizations remain responsible for policy decisions, ownership, testing, and ongoing review. Recommended next steps Open Dataverse capacity reporting and identify the environments and tables using the most database, file, and log storage. Assign a business owner to each material source of growth and classify the data as active, inactive but required, or eligible for deletion. Test one control in a nonproduction environment. Options include a long-term retention policy , a revised security role , a scoped audit configuration , or a 1-to-30-day deleted-record recovery window . Document the owner, policy basis, expected capacity or risk outcome, test result, and recovery procedure. Prepare the data foundation for AI AI increases the number of automated processes that use business data and the frequency with which that data changes. Capacity management, retention, access control, auditing, and recovery should therefore be reviewed as part of every production AI deployment that uses Dataverse. Organizations can begin with the controls already available in Dataverse. A documented operating process, clear ownership, and regular review provide the foundation for broader AI adoption. Learn more: Review capacity reporting , long-term retention , security roles , auditing , deleted-record recovery , and managed governance .

title: Cementos Argos’ results steady in first half of 2026

title: Can You Borrow Against Stocks and Mutual Funds in One Account?
summary: Learn how investors should think about borrowing against stocks and mutual funds, what to check, and why selling is not the only way to raise cash.
body_text: Can You Borrow Against Stocks and Mutual Funds in One Account? Intro If your investments are split across stocks and mutual funds, a cash need can create an awkward question: do you have to sell something, or can the portfolio help you borrow without disturbing your long-term plan? The useful answer is not “all investments qualify” or “sell first.” The useful answer is: check which holdings are eligible, understand the pledge terms, and compare borrowing with selling before you make a permanent portfolio move. A mixed portfolio can still be a source of liquidity. But eligibility depends on the specific holdings and the lender or platform flow, so you should not assume every stock or mutual fund can automatically support a loan. Key Takeaways A mixed portfolio does not automatically mean you must sell assets to raise cash. Eligibility depends on the specific stocks, mutual funds, and lender/platform rules. Borrowing can be better than selling when you need liquidity but still want the investments to remain part of your plan. Check charges, repayment comfort, collateral-value risk, and pledge-release rules before drawing money. The short answer: check eligible holdings before you sell You may be able to borrow against eligible investments instead of selling them, but the first step is always eligibility. Stocks and mutual funds are not all treated the same. Some holdings may qualify, some may not, and the amount you can borrow can vary based on the asset type, portfolio value, and lender rules. That is why a mixed portfolio should trigger a check, not a quick sale. A portfolio-backed loan starts with what can safely be pledged, not with selling by default. With Yenmo, eligible investors can check options across lending partners through one platform. That matters when your holdings are spread across different investment types and you want a cleaner way to understand what is usable for liquidity. Why mixed portfolios create confusion Mixed portfolios feel confusing because investors often think in terms of “my total investments,” while lenders think in terms of eligible collateral. You may own a stock that is valuable but not eligible in a particular loan flow. You may own mutual funds that can be pledged, while other holdings need a different treatment. You may also have assets across brokers, demat accounts, or investment platforms. Owning investments and being able to pledge them are related, but not identical. That difference is important because it protects you from overestimating liquidity. If you need ₹3 lakh, for example, you should not assume every rupee of portfolio value can be turned into a borrowing limit. The right approach is to check eligibility first, then decide whether borrowing, partial selling, or another option fits. When can borrowing be better than selling? Borrowing can be better than selling when the investment still belongs in your long-term plan. If you sell stocks or redeem mutual funds for a cash need, you get certainty. But you also reduce the portfolio that was meant to compound or participate in future market movement. You may also need to consider tax, exit load for some funds, brokerage, or the difficulty of rebuilding the same position later. Borrowing works differently. You use eligible investments as collateral, access cash, and aim to keep the asset in place while you repay. That can be valuable when the need is real but the portfolio should not be interrupted. The cost of selling is not only today’s cash. It can be the future exposure you give up. This is why the borrow-versus-sell comparison matters. If you need money but still believe in the investments, selling should not be the automatic answer. Yenmo’s loan against mutual fund calculator vs redemption calculator can help you think through that trade-off for mutual fund holdings. What changes after you pledge investments? Pledging is not the same as selling, but it does change flexibility. When an eligible asset is pledged, it supports the loan. You should not treat pledged holdings like completely free holdings that can be moved, sold, or redeemed whenever you want. The asset may still move with the market, but it is also part of the borrowing arrangement. Still invested does not mean unrestricted. That distinction keeps the decision honest. Borrowing can preserve investment exposure, but it also creates a responsibility: repay comfortably, monitor the facility, and understand what happens if collateral value changes. How should you compare a mixed-portfolio loan with selling assets? Use a practical framework rather than a single yes-or-no rule. 1. Which holdings are actually eligible? Start with eligibility. Do not plan your cash flow around assets until you know whether they can support borrowing in the platform or lender flow. 2. Do you still want to own the assets? If an investment no longer fits your goals, selling may be reasonable. If you still want to hold it, borrowing deserves a closer look. 3. How much do you need to withdraw? A credit-line style product is most useful when you borrow according to the actual need. With Yenmo’s loan-against-mutual-funds structure, interest is charged only on the amount withdrawn, not simply on the full eligible limit. 4. Can you leave a buffer? Market-linked collateral can move. Yenmo’s guidance is that borrowers should usually leave roughly a 10% buffer when withdrawing, so normal market movement is less likely to create a shortfall. 5. What happens if the value falls? If portfolio value falls after you have already drawn money, the eligible amount can reduce. Lenders generally give about 7 days to fix a shortfall by repaying part of the outstanding amount or pledging more mutual funds. What should you check before using stocks and mutual funds as collateral? Before you borrow, ask direct questions. Which stocks or mutual funds are eligible? What borrowing limit is available against the eligible holdings? Is interest charged on the full limit or only on what you withdraw? Are there any hidden charges, foreclosure charges, or prepayment penalties? What restrictions apply to pledged holdings? How do you release or unpledge assets after repayment? What happens if market value falls? The safest borrowing decision is the one you understand before you tap the limit. Yenmo highlights no hidden charges, no foreclosure charges, and no prepayment penalties in its core loan-against-mutual-funds offer. Still, review the terms shown to you before accepting any offer. When should you sell instead? Selling may be better when repayment would be stressful, when the investment no longer fits your portfolio, or when you need total simplicity and immediate freedom over the asset. Borrowing is not automatically superior just because you own investments. It works best when the cash need is manageable, the eligible holdings are suitable, and you are comfortable with the loan structure. If you would need to withdraw the maximum available limit with no buffer, pause. A portfolio-backed loan should make your liquidity decision calmer, not more fragile. How Yenmo fits this decision Yenmo is built for investors who need liquidity but do not want selling to be the first answer. For eligible mutual fund investors, Yenmo helps you pledge instead of redeeming, check eligibility through an app-led flow, and borrow while keeping the investment decision separate from the cash need. The trust ecosystem includes CAMS, KFin, NSDL, DigiLocker, lending partners such as Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital, and DSP Finance, and Y Combinator backing. If your holdings include both stocks and mutual funds, start with a calm eligibility check. Then compare the cost of borrowing with the cost of selling the assets you still want to own. FAQ Can I borrow against both stocks and mutual funds? You may be able to use eligible investments as collateral, but eligibility depends on the specific holdings and lender/platform rules. Check the exact eligible amount before planning your withdrawal. Are all stocks and mutual funds eligible? No. Do not assume every holding qualifies. Eligibility can vary, so the app or lender flow should confirm what can actually be pledged. Do investments keep moving after pledging? Pledged investments can still be exposed to market movement because pledging is different from selling. But pledged assets are restricted while they support the loan. Should I sell weak holdings instead? If an investment no longer fits your portfolio, selling can be reasonable. Borrowing is more useful when you want to keep the asset invested. What is the main risk of borrowing against a mixed portfolio? The main risks are repayment pressure, interest cost, and collateral-value movement. Borrow only when the facility remains comfortable even if markets move. Conclusion A mixed portfolio should not push you into a rushed sale. If you need cash, first check which stocks or mutual funds are eligible, what limit is available, and whether repayment is comfortable. Selling may still be right in some cases. But when you want to stay invested, borrowing against eligible holdings can be a smarter comparison. Before you sell assets you still believe in, check your eligibility with Yenmo and see whether a pledge-backed option can solve the cash need with less portfolio disruption.

title: Architecture is fundamentally a human endeavor says panel during AIA conference
summary: At an AIA conference panel, architecture leaders explored how AI can accelerate design while human judgment, storytelling and creativity remain central.
body_text: By Sonia Singh, Dezeen This article was written and originally published in July 2026 by Dezeen, the leading online architecture, interiors and design magazine. Published with permission. Human judgement and storytelling should remain central to architecture as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in the design process, according to a panel hosted by Trimble SketchUp and Dezeen in San Diego during AIA. Christopher Cronin, senior vice president of architecture and design solutions at Trimble, was on the panel for “The Productive Architect: How AI is Changing Our Approach to Design”. The panellists explored the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) in architectural practice, arguing that while it can complement the design process and improve productivity, human interaction and ingenuity must remain at the forefront. Taking a step back and adding critical thinking "Fundamentally, architecture is a human endeavour," said Perkins Eastman design principal Omar Calderon Santiago. Despite the rapid pace of AI development, Calderon Santiago argued that speed does not always equate to value or quality, encouraging architects to take a step back and approach each project with critical thinking. Dezeen co-CEO Benedict Hobson (second from left) moderated the session. The panel included Omar Calderon Santiago (left), Marissa Ritchen and Christopher Cronin (right). "With the speed of things, it's very easy to rabbit hole yourself," he said. "I think we need to slow down and try to get back to the root of what we're trying to do." He explained that he begins projects with hand sketches before introducing AI into his workflow, using the technology to develop ideas rather than generate them. "I use that as the point of departure to then help AI boost the story that I'm trying to tell," he said Calderon Santiago also reflected on the importance of maintaining a human connection throughout the design process, recalling a client presentation where he deliberately chose hand drawings over polished renderings. "This individual connected with us at a human level, because he was seeing in these drawings something that someone had taken the time to make," he said. Architects are storytellers The panellists also discussed how AI can remove repetitive tasks, allowing architects to spend more time refining ideas and solving complex design challenges. Licensed architect and Kestrel Labs chief industry officer Marissa Ritchen cited her company's code compliance platform as an example of AI being used to automate time-consuming processes. She said the technology should create more time for storytelling and creative exploration rather than replace them. "I think an architect will always be a storyteller," she said. "That idea of lived experience will always inform the architect. You're bringing all of your lived experiences and you are distilling them, and bringing folks in and inviting them into a space that they're collaborating on." Technology suppliers must stay agile Christopher Cronin, senior vice president of architecture and design at SketchUp and education at Trimble, described how he is approaching the rapid pace of AI development. "You have to be very nimble," Cronin said. "AI 3D model and image generation capabilities are moving incredibly quickly. We as a company need to stay on top of it and test and adopt the new models as soon as they come out." He shared how tools such as the SketchUp Connector for Claude , an AI-driven MCP integration that generates 3D models through natural language, are already changing the design process.

title: Best Buy appoints Anne Bramman as chief financial officer
summary: Prior to joining Best Buy, Bramman held leadership roles at numerous consumer, technology and industrial organizations.
body_text: By Best Buy August 3, 2026 Key Highlights Seasoned executive : Bramman, a veteran Fortune 500 executive, brings deep retail, consumer and operation finance expertise to Best Buy. Executive leadership team : She will join the executive leadership team under Jason Bonfig, who will succeed Corie Barry as chief executive officer on Nov. 1. Effective date : Bramman will join Best Buy on Aug. 19. Best Buy announced today the appointment of Anne Bramman as executive vice president and chief financial officer, effective Aug. 19. Bramman joins Best Buy as a seasoned public company executive with more than 30 years of leadership experience across finance, operations, strategy and transformation. In her new role, she will lead Best Buy’s global finance organization and help drive the company’s strategic priorities in partnership with incoming Chief Executive Officer Jason Bonfig and the rest of the leadership team. “Anne brings an impressive and unique combination of finance and operations experience that aligns perfectly with Best Buy and where we’re headed,” Bonfig said. “Her consumer expertise, along with her proven track record of leading teams and creating long-term shareholder value will be instrumental as we take on our next chapter.” “I’ve long admired Best Buy’s ability to adapt, innovate and stay deeply connected to its customers,” said Bramman. “I’m thrilled to join the company and I look forward to working with Jason and the impressive Best Buy team to help accelerate growth and build an exciting future together.” Prior to joining Best Buy, Bramman held leadership roles at numerous consumer, technology and industrial organizations. She most recently served as chief financial and growth officer of Circana, a leading consumer analytics company. Prior to Circana, Bramman was CFO of Nordstrom, leading the company’s financial strategy, capital allocation and digital transformation efforts. She also served as CFO of Avery Dennison and Carnival Cruise Line and held senior finance leadership roles at L Brands. Today, she serves on the boards of Morningstar and McCormick & Company. Bramman will report to Bonfig and serve on his executive leadership team as the company continues its CEO transition. Bonfig will succeed current CEO Corie Barry on Nov. 1. body_text: Australian golf prodigy Jessica Bang has died aged 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage while preparing for a tournament in Thailand. Read about her rising career, achievements and tributes. Australian golf has been left mourning the sudden death of rising star Jessica Bang, who passed away at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage while preparing for a tournament in Thailand. Bang collapsed on August 1 while in Bangkok and was taken to hospital for emergency treatment. She underwent brain surgery and spent almost two weeks in intensive care before her death on Thursday, August 13. Her passing has prompted an outpouring of grief from her family, fellow golfers and the wider Australian sporting community. The teenager had been building an exciting career in professional golf and was regarded as one of Australia's promising young talents. Her death has brought an abrupt end to a career that had only recently begun but had already produced several significant achievements. Jessica Bang collapsed while preparing for a tournament Bang was in Thailand as she prepared for an international qualifying event connected with the Korean women's professional golf tour. According to reports, she suddenly collapsed on August 1 after suffering a brain haemorrhage. She was rushed to a hospital in Bangkok, where doctors performed emergency brain surgery. Bang remained in intensive care for almost two weeks as her family and friends hoped she would recover. Despite the medical team's efforts, Bang died on August 13. The news has shocked the golf community because of her age and the speed with which her promising sporting career was cut short. Reports from multiple outlets have confirmed the circumstances surrounding her illness and death. A remarkable start to her professional golf career Jessica Bang had only recently entered professional golf, but she had already made a strong impression. She earned her place on the WPGA Tour of Australasia through qualifying school at the end of 2025. Her progression followed an impressive amateur career, which included victory in the Queensland Amateur. Earlier in 2026, Bang produced one of the biggest results of her young career when she won the Ford Women's NSW Open Regional Qualifying Event at Moss Vale. Remarkably, it was only her fifth professional start. Her victory demonstrated the potential that had made Bang such an exciting prospect in Australian golf. She had quickly moved from promising amateur to professional winner, suggesting that she could have enjoyed a long and successful career in the sport. WPGA Tour pays tribute to Jessica Bang The WPGA Tour of Australasia expressed its deep sadness following Bang's death and paid tribute to her ability and character. The organisation described her as an "outstanding young talent" who had made a significant impression during her short time on the professional tour. The tribute reflected the sense of loss within Australian golf. The fundraiser was created to help Bang's parents with medical costs following her sudden illness in Thailand. It had raised close to A$50,000, equivalent to around £26,000, according to reports. The family's comments have added a deeply personal dimension to the story. Beyond her achievements on the golf course, Bang was a daughter, cousin, friend and young woman whose life extended far beyond sport. A promising career cut tragically short Jessica Bang's story is particularly poignant because of how quickly her professional career had begun to develop. After qualifying for the WPGA Tour, she immediately showed that she could compete at a high level. Winning a professional event in only her fifth start was an extraordinary achievement for an 18-year-old golfer. Her progress also demonstrated the strength of the pathway from amateur golf to the professional game. Bang had already achieved success at amateur level before taking the next step, and her early professional victory suggested she was capable of competing against more experienced players. The tournament in Thailand was another opportunity for her to continue that development. Instead, it became the setting for the medical emergency that ultimately claimed her life. For many who followed her early career, her death represents the loss of a player who had only just begun to show what she might achieve. Her achievements may have come in a short period, but they left a lasting impression on those who watched her compete. While her final days were marked by a devastating medical emergency, her legacy will also be shaped by her determination, sporting achievements and love of golf. Remembering Jessica Bang Jessica Bang died at just 18, at a point when her professional career appeared to be gathering momentum. Her first professional victory, qualification for the WPGA Tour and successful amateur career offered a glimpse of what could have been a remarkable future in golf. Instead, her life was tragically cut short following a brain haemorrhage in Thailand. The Australian golfing community now remembers Bang not only as a talented young professional but as a person whose enthusiasm, humour and dedication touched those around her. title: Calculating Self-Employed Income With an AI Agent: The 1084 Cash-Flow Analysis, the 4506-C Transcript, and the Reasonableness Call the Underwriter Owns
summary: Self-employed income is where mortgage underwriting is slowest, most inconsistent, and most exposed to fair-lending risk, because two underwriters can read the same tax returns and reach different qualifying income. An AI agent can run the Form 1084 cash-flow analysis the same way every time and document every add-back to its line on the return. What it cannot do is make the reasonableness determination Fannie assigns to the underwriter, and building the agent so it stops at that line is the whole design problem.
